\begin{proof}
\begin{enumerate}[label={$\langle1\rangle$\arabic*.},leftmargin=*]
\item \emph{The geometric meaning of the new weights.}
Iteration of the original lifted translation replaces
its line multiplier by the product of its first $d$
translates. If its initial zero is one component of
$I_n$, the new zero is its orbit sum, with repetitions.
It need not be a whole fibre. This is the prescribed
norm linearization, so no unsupported line-bundle
modification is being introduced.
Outside the finite replacements the new space is
the connected gamma cover defined by $S_d$ of the
old original or Mumford model. It follows directly
that the good-reduction monodromies are \eqref{maps:eq:D.WP2};
the same construction on their root discs permits
all the new free finite quotients.

\item At the unique rank-two zero the old valuation
lattice was the full short lattice. Multiplying
one long period by $d$ gives index $d$. The same
smooth triangular fan therefore has $d$ copies
of the old normalized $dP_6$ in its quotient.
At a zero-free rank-one site, write the old
monodromy as $I+\alpha\beta^*$ with $\alpha$
primitive and $\beta^*$ primitive. The cover
replaces $\beta^*$ by $\beta^*S_d$.
The exact factorization certificate retains all $436$
zero-free rank-one matrices as $\alpha\beta^*$, with
both vectors primitive. If $P$ is narrow, the content
of the first three entries of $\beta^*$ is exactly
$n_i$, and its gamma entry is prime to $n_i$. Thus
the new content is $\gcd(d,n_i)$. At every non-narrow
$P$ site that vertical content is exactly one, so
its new content is one for every $d$. These actual
vectors and entries are recorded in
\path{records/manifolds_weighted_rankone_certificates.json}.
Thus the respective component counts are precisely
those in the statement. This also follows directly
by lifting the component cycle through the gamma
cover. Zero-degree original multiplicative caps
have the same component count and the same global
kernel image; no relative diffeomorphism is asserted.

\item An original zero-degree additive cap is
$S^1_\delta$ times the mapping torus of the Kodaira
tree under $Q^d$. It has $\rho_i(d)$ fundamental
component cycles. At a nonzero-Chern original, $Q$
was already narrow and remains narrow; its
primitive Chern vector is unchanged. Its component
count and its principal-torus description from
\ref{maps:src:D.2.32} or \ref{maps:src:D.2.33} are therefore unchanged.
All these caps have torsion-free top homology and
Euler number zero. The rank-two cusp has Euler
number $2d$ by its normalization complex.

\item \emph{Why the regular integral lattice is free in the stated sector.}
For each original row, \ref{maps:src:D.2.23} gives
\[
 \Lambda_{\{A_i\}}=\mathbb Z\gamma,\qquad
 (\Lambda^2\Lambda)_{\{A_i\}}=\mathbb Zs,
\]
with primitive functional \eqref{maps:eq:D.WP3} at $d=1$.
There is a finite exact certificate for all other
weights. Set $d=0$ in the polynomial matrices
\eqref{maps:eq:D.WP2}, meaning that their first three gamma
entries are zero. For every one of the $172$ rows
the common degree-one relation matrix still has
rank three, the degree-two matrix has rank five,
and every prime in their nonunit Smith factors
divides $a$. The complete constant matrices and
Smith factors are retained in
\path{records/manifolds_weighted_zero_certificates.json}.

\item Here is why this finite certificate proves the
unbounded claim. At a prime not dividing $d$,
$S_d$ is an integral local isomorphism, so the
relations have the original saturated ranks.
At a prime dividing $d$, condition \eqref{maps:eq:D.WP1} makes
$a$ a unit, and reduction modulo that prime is
the just-certified $d=0$ matrix, still of full
rank three or five. Hence no prime divides a
nonunit Smith factor at the new weight.
The two common coinvariants are therefore free
of ranks one and one for every allowed $d$.
Moreover \eqref{maps:eq:D.WP3} is primitive since
$\gcd(a,db)=1$, so it is their actual integral
degree-two functional.

\item The graph Serre sequence consequently gives
\[
 H_1(V)=\mathbb Z\gamma\oplus\mathbb Z^{N-1},
 \qquad H_2(V)=\mathbb Zs\oplus K.                         \tag{D.WP10}\hypertarget{tag-027P}{}\label{maps:eq:D.WP10}
\]
The splitting used in \eqref{maps:eq:D.WP10} is marked. On the
original regular piece the integral fibre class
has value zero on every fixed-loop peripheral
sweep, by the unrolled comparison and the single
diagonal relation of \ref{maps:src:D.2.23}--\ref{maps:src:D.2.26}. Pull it back
through the actual gamma cover. It restricts to
$\omega_d$ and still has value zero on every
new fixed sweep: that sweep maps to the old
sweep of $S_d\lambda$.
Primitivity of $\omega_d$ makes this a genuine
integral splitting. This is a pullback of an
already marked class, not an assumption that
an invariant differential form descends integrally.

\item \emph{All local boundary-kernel images.}
For a finite-good matrix, all nonidentity linear
powers have the same fixed real two-plane.
Its projected lattice is
$P\Lambda=(N_h/h)\Lambda=F(H/h)\mathbb Z^2$.
The translation $v/m$ on that quotient has exact
order $m/t$. A nonidentity linear power can have
a fixed point exactly when its exponent is
divisible by $m/t$. Requiring all such exponents
to have identity linear part is $h\mid m/t$.
For the identity-linear powers one must additionally
have the full translation of order $m$, which is
the primitive-vector condition in \eqref{maps:eq:D.WP5}.
This proves the stated freeness criterion for
arbitrary coordinates and orders.

\item The full normal Thom image is generated by the
four covering-torus loops and the affine meridian.
The cut of their swept normal tori into the regular
fibre is respectively $N_m\lambda$ and $v$.
Integration of the actual pulled-back marked
class from \eqref{maps:eq:D.WP10} gives respectively
$-\omega_d(\lambda,v)$ and zero, exactly as in
\ref{maps:src:D.2.29}. These are complete integral coordinates
in the free target \eqref{maps:eq:D.WP10}, so a local torsion
ambiguity cannot be lost by this computation.
In particular no claim of integral form descent
on the finite quotient is needed.
This proves \eqref{maps:eq:D.WP6}, including finite cap and
normal-line torsion.

\item For a Mumford or zero-degree original cap, every
new fixed normal torus bounds. Its image under
the covering is an old fixed normal torus; the
old bounding section-disc sweep lifts because
its loop is in the covering lattice. Equivalently
use the same toric or Neron-logarithm section
disc and its actual invariant circle actions.
These are all the normal projections, since
the Wang projection takes values in the full
fixed lattice.
After subtracting them, any further kernel
element comes from a fibre class. Rationally
its image is zero exactly on the monodromy-image
subspace. At the rank-two zero, the two primitive
angular normal tori exhaust the boundary kernel:
$H_2(\partial N)=\mathbb Z^6$ and
$H^3(N)=\mathbb Z^2$ by \ref{maps:src:D.2.34}. The regular-fibre
coinvariant of rank four therefore injects. At a
rank-one cap the nodal cycle times $T^2$ supplies
four independent fibre images (whole fibre, two
mixed surviving-circle tori, and transverse area).
At an original zero-degree additive cap the
Kodaira-tree permutation model supplies the whole
fibre and the transverse area, the full two
dimensional coinvariant. These explicit models
prove the required ranks for every weight.
The functional $\omega_d$ annihilates that
subspace. Since the global fibre coinvariant
in \eqref{maps:eq:D.WP10} is free, every such fibre-kernel
class has zero global image, even when it is
torsion in the boundary. This proves the entire
global image \eqref{maps:eq:D.WP7}.

\item For a nonzero-Chern original, the marked logarithm
vectors scale by $d$. The exact area-kernel
calculations of \ref{maps:src:D.2.32}--\ref{maps:src:D.2.33} therefore multiply
their fibre values by $d$, giving $dh_i\mathbb Zs$.
Their complete fixed normal projections still
bound, and the third multiplicative correction
is still annihilated by $\omega_d$.
This proves the remaining column, integrally.

\item \emph{The relative sequence and the free component contribution.}
First attach only the finite and regular logarithmic
caps to $V$, and call the result $E$. There is at
least one unfilled cap, the rank-two zero.
The relative degree-two group of each attached
disc bundle is $\mathbb Z$, whose boundary has
its nonzero multiplicity in its independent base
meridian coordinate. These relative maps into
$H_1(V)$ are injective. Thus $H_2(E)$ is exactly
the quotient of \eqref{maps:eq:D.WP10} by their full Thom
images, including when the cap has torsion.

\item Now attach all the remaining original and Mumford
caps $N_j$. Their relative degree-two groups are
\[
 H_2(N_j,\partial N_j)=H^4(N_j),
\]
free on their fundamental component cycles.
The degree-three boundary images are exactly
the kernels already computed above. Consequently
the pair sequence has the form
\[
 0\longrightarrow\operatorname{coker}B
 \longrightarrow H_2(X)
 \longrightarrow
 \ker\!\left\{\bigoplus_j H^4(N_j)\to H_1(E)\right\}
 \longrightarrow0.                                      \tag{D.WP11}\hypertarget{tag-027Q}{}\label{maps:eq:D.WP11}
\]
Its last group is a subgroup of a free group,
so the sequence splits as a sequence of abelian
groups. This avoids all potentially nonprimitive
degree-one boundary splittings.

\item If there are $s$ unfilled caps, $H_1(E)$ has free
rank $s$: the finite/regular power relations
remove their independent base directions.
The final rank is $r$, so the map in \eqref{maps:eq:D.WP11}
has rank $s-r$. Its domain has rank equal to
the sum of the component counts. Subtracting
one per cap gives
\[
 \operatorname{rank}\ker
   =d-1+\beta+L+r.                                        \tag{D.WP12}\hypertarget{tag-027R}{}\label{maps:eq:D.WP12}
\]
This is an exact rank calculation in a free
relative group; torsion meridians can change
its index but cannot change its freeness or
introduce an extension in \eqref{maps:eq:D.WP11}.

\item Over the rationals \eqref{maps:eq:D.WP2} is conjugate to the

\emph{Every finite-good affine logarithm and its full kernel.}

This section applies to II, III, IV, \(\mathrm{III}^*\), \(\mathrm{IV}^*\), whose linear
orders h are respectively 6,4,3,4,3. The odd \(I_n^*\) caps remain
original. The all-star-original subset is described in the enumeration.

Let \(A=A_i(d)\), let F be any primitive integral basis of
\(\Lambda^A\), and let \(N_h=I+A+\cdots+A^{h-1}\).
Its image lies in \(\Lambda^A\). Let H be an integral basis
matrix of the image of \(F^{-1}N_h\), and put
\[
 Q=H^{-1}F^{-1}N_h:\Lambda\longrightarrow\mathbb Z^2.
\]
The definition of H makes Q surjective. A Bézout sum of its
maximal-minor adjugates gives an integral section \(R_\pi\)
with \(QR_\pi=I\).
Because \(N_hF=hF\), the matrix \(hH^{-1}\) is integral.
The fixed-plane projection and its projected lattice are
\[
 P=N_h/h,\qquad
 P\Lambda=F(H/h)\mathbb Z^2.
\]
Thus the displayed projection, the Q coordinates, and \(R_\pi\)
give both inverse maps for the projected lattice.

For an invariant integral power \(v=Fz\) and \(m=hk>0\), put
\[
             w=hH^{-1}z=Qv,\qquad t=\gcd(m,w_1,w_2).
\]
Every affine action with that power is conjugate to
\(f(x)=Ax+v/m\) on the central real torus. Indeed the
difference of its translation and v/m lies in \(\ker P\), and
translation by \((I-A)^{-1}\) of that difference gives the
conjugacy; translation by its negative gives its inverse.

This comparison extends on the good-reduction root
disc. Let R be the finite deck operator on holomorphic Lie
sections, \(R^m=I\). After matching the same integral power,
the difference \(b_0\) of two affine lifts satisfies \(Nb_0=0\).
Set
\[
 h_0=-\frac1m\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}jR^j b_0.
\]
The identity \((I-R)\sum jR^j=N-mI\) gives
\((I-R)h_0=b_0\). Translation by \(h_0\) and by -\(h_0\) are
inverse holomorphic maps across the centre. A universal
lift change by a period \(\lambda\) changes the power by \(N_m\lambda\). This is the exact norm convention used here.

\emph{Every-power freeness.}

The moving plane of A has a primitive h-th root pair as
its eigenvalues. Consequently \(A^j-I\) is invertible on
\(\ker P\) whenever h does not divide j. Its fixed-point
equation is soluble exactly when
\[
                  jv/m\in P\Lambda.
\]
For necessity apply P to the equation. For sufficiency choose
\(\lambda=R_\pi(jw/m)\) in \(\Lambda\), and solve
\[
 x=(A^j-I)^{-1}(\lambda-jv/m)
\]
on \(\ker P\). The chosen \(\lambda\) has the required projection by
the projection and its section; substitution proves the equation. Thus the
obstruction indices are exactly the positive multiples
of m/t.

Let \(u=\gcd(m,v_1,v_2,v_3,v_4)\). For \(u>1\) the power m/u
has an integral translation, so \(x=0\) is a fixed point of
its linear part. For \(u=1\), every proper power divisible
by h has identity linear part and nonintegral translation.
All remaining obstruction indices are divisible by h
exactly when \(h\mid m/t\). We have therefore proved, for
every positive order and every invariant integral vector,
\[
 f\text{ is free}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \gcd(m,v_1,v_2,v_3,v_4)=1,\quad h\mid m/t.
\]
For a free action, each nonidentity element has closed
fixed set disjoint from the compact central torus.
A sufficiently small common root neighbourhood is
therefore free for all those elements. The conjugacy
above carries this conclusion to the original affine
lift on that neighbourhood.

\emph{The torsion and the normal character.}

Using the conjugacy \(A(d)H_d=H_dA(1)\), the two nonzero Smith entries of \(A-I\) are units.
The kernel of Q is the image of \(A-I\): both are primitive rank-two
subgroups, and \(Q(A-I)=0\). Equivalently
\(\operatorname{im}(I-R_\pi Q)=\operatorname{im}(A-I)\);
the projector gives its integer image and inverse coordinates. The central
quotient \(F_0\) has the affine group with generators
\(\Lambda\) and c, relations
\(c\lambda c^{-1}=A\lambda\), \(c^m=v\). Abelianization
and the map \(Q=H^{-1}F^{-1}N_h\) give
\[
 H_1(F_0)=
 (\mathbb Z^2\oplus\mathbb Zc)/
          \langle(-w_1,-w_2,m)\rangle
       =\mathbb Z^2\oplus\mathbb Z/t.
\]
A Bézout completion of \((-w_1,-w_2,m)/t\) gives the
forward Smith coordinates and inverse. The torsion
generator is this primitive vector modulo its t-fold
multiple.

The root normal character is zero on \(\Lambda\) and 1/m
on c.~Its value on that torsion generator is 1/t.
Its Bockstein is the integral normal Chern class;
therefore that class has exact order t and no free
component. The finite torus cover, followed by averaging
its exterior forms, gives rational Betti numbers
\((1,2,2,2,1)\). Integral duality and UCT give
\[
 H_*(F_0)=
 (\mathbb Z,\ \mathbb Z^2\oplus\mathbb Z/t,\
  \mathbb Z^2\oplus\mathbb Z/t,\ \mathbb Z^2,\ \mathbb Z).
\]
The torsion identification sends a coordinate k to the
character \(j\mapsto kj/t\); evaluation at its generator
is the inverse. Thus this duality step retains the exact
torsion coordinate.

\emph{Full normal Thom columns, including the root generator.}

The normal disk bundle U retracts onto \(F_0\). Its boundary
is identified with the mapping torus of A by
\[
 [y,\tau]\longmapsto
 [\,y+(\tau/m)v,\ \exp(2\pi i\tau/m)\,].
\]
The relation \((y,\tau)\sim(Ay,\tau+1)\) becomes exactly
the affine deck relation. The inverse chooses a root
argument \(\tau\) and subtracts \((\tau/m)v\); a change of
argument gives that same mapping-torus relation.
The positive normal circle is
\((y,\tau)\mapsto(y-sv,\tau+ms)\).

For a lattice loop \(\lambda\), cut its normal torus into the
m root sectors. Its positive fixed sweep is \(N_m\lambda\);
its fibre parallelogram is \(-\lambda\wedge v\). Rejoining
the sectors along their marked A-edges is the inverse
chain map. For the core loop c, use the parametrization
\[
 [\,uv/m,\ \exp(2\pi i(u/m+t))\,].
\]
Its coordinates in the root boundary map are \(y=-tv,\ \tau=u+mt\).
Its fixed sweep is v and its vertical area is zero.
These are the normal tori of all generators of \(H_1(F_0)\).
They therefore give exactly the five global columns
\[
 \bigl(-\omega_d(\lambda,v),J_iN_m\lambda\bigr)
      \quad(\lambda=e_1,e_2,\delta,\gamma),\qquad
                      (0,J_iv).
\]
For \(\lambda\) in \((A-I)\Lambda\), both entries vanish:
\(N_m(A-I)=0\) and invariance of \(\omega_d\) with Av=v
gives \(\omega_d((A-I)\lambda,v)=0\).
Thus \eqref{maps:eq:D.WP6} factors through the full coinvariant group,
and the inverse section \(R_\pi\) recovers the two essential
lattice generators with the root column included.

For an explicit relation, set \(\lambda_j=R_\pi e_j\).
Then \(R_\pi w-v\in(A-I)\Lambda\), so
\(N_mR_\pi w=mv\) and \(\omega_d(R_\pi w,v)=0\).

these identities give the exact primitive relation
\[
 (m/t)K_c-(w_1/t)K_{\lambda_1}-(w_2/t)K_{\lambda_2}=0.
\]
The two norm projections of \(\lambda_1\) and \(\lambda_2\) are
independent, so their three-column kernel has rank one.
The displayed coefficients have gcd one, hence they
generate that full integral relation lattice. The Q
and \(R_\pi\) maps express every original lattice column
in these two coordinates, with inverse modulo \(A-I\).

The boundary \(H_2\) is free, since its four wedge Smith
entries are units by the conjugacy \(A(d)H_d=H_dA(1)\), while its fixed lattice is
free of rank two. Its Thom map consequently kills the
torsion generator in the displayed presentation of \(H_1(F_0)\); its explicit linear
combination of columns is zero. This proves the exact relation in the normal map from the full core group.

Cap product \(H_2(F_0)\to H_0(F_0)\) with the torsion
normal Chern class is zero. The Thom sequence therefore
makes the boundary \(H_2\) map onto all of \(H_2(F_0)\), including

image \eqref{maps:eq:D.WP6}. Thus a finite-good cap has no separate
free degree-two defect. The global elimination in
the relative attachment argument uses this surjection with its kernel and
retains its torsion.

\emph{Regular logarithms and clutch.}

At a regular site \(A=I\). The affine action is translation
by v/m, and its every-power freeness is exactly
\(\gcd(m,v_1,v_2,v_3,v_4)=1\). The quotient is the
torus with lattice \(\Lambda+\mathbb Z(v/m)\);
its inverse is the same real vector modulo that lattice.
The root boundary map and its inverse remain
valid, and the full kernel is \eqref{maps:eq:D.WP6} with \(N_m=mI\).
A Bézout completion of \((-v,m)\) supplies the integral
quotient coordinates. Primitivity of this vector makes the core homology free.

An extra order-one regular logarithm with \(v_*=-e\gamma\)
encodes any integer peripheral clutch. The boundary shear is
\[
 (y,\theta)\longmapsto(y-\theta v_*,\theta),
\]
with inverse plus \(\theta\) \(v_*\). Its Seifert generator is
\(c_*=\gamma^{-e}\), so deleting it from the product-one
relation gives the required product \(\gamma^e\).
The four unit normal relations eliminate its fixed
sweeps by
\[
                 t_*(u)=\omega_d(u,v_*)s.
\]
In particular \(t_*(\delta)=db\,e\,s\); its remaining
root column follows because \(\omega_d(v_*,v_*)=0\).
The inverse inserts these four sweep coordinates.
This proves the clutch convention for every e,
including zero and negative integers.

More generally, changing a finite peripheral lift by
\(\lambda\) changes v to \(v+N_m\lambda\). The normal sweep
map changes by \(t'_i(u)=t_i(u)+\omega_d(u,\lambda)s\);
the inverse subtracts this value. Invariance gives
\(N_m^t\omega_d=\omega_dN_m\) and
\(\omega_d(N_m\lambda,\lambda)=0\). Substitution in
\eqref{maps:eq:D.WP6} verifies every relation under these maps.
At a regular site this reduces to \(v\mapsto v+m\lambda\).
The norm morphism is the change of peripheral power in both cases.

  the additive value \(\omega_d(k_d)=-db/q\) and the multiplicative value \(\omega_d(k_d)=-db/\nu\).
\item
  At every finite or regular logarithm use all five
  columns \eqref{maps:eq:D.WP6}, with its order and power vector.
\end{enumerate}

These are \eqref{maps:eq:D.WP6}--\eqref{maps:eq:D.WP7}, evaluated in the primitive graph coordinates.
Let \(C_d=\operatorname{coker}B\) and \(T=\operatorname{Tor}C_d\).

Attach the k finite or regular logarithmic caps to V and call the
result E. At least the cusp remains unfilled; write
\(s_{\mathrm{unf}}=N-k\) for the number of unfilled caps.
Choose one unfilled base loop as the
omitted bouquet edge. The integral relative group of each attached
normal disc bundle in degree two is \(H_0\) of its connected core,
namely Z. Write \(x_i\) for the positive base meridian at site i.
A positive normal disc maps to
\[
                         m_ix_i-v_i
\]
in \(H_1\) of its boundary. In \(H_1(V)\), the vertical coordinates vanish
and its \(\gamma\) coordinate is \(-\chi(v_i)\). The resulting relative
boundary columns are
\[
                  m_ix_i-\chi(v_i)\gamma .
\]
Each has its own nonzero base coefficient \(m_i>0\). Their map to
the free group \(H_1(V)=\mathbb Z\gamma\oplus\mathbb Z^{N-1}\)
is injective. The inverse on its image reads the corresponding
base coordinate and divides by \(m_i\). Excision and the Thom
sequence consequently give
\[
 H_2(E)=H_2(V)/(\text{all finite and regular Thom images}),
\]
with the five columns at each site, including the root generator.
The full group \(H_1(E)\) retains the presentation by those power
columns and the one base relation; its free rank is \(s_{\mathrm{unf}}\).

For each remaining original or Mumford cap \(U_j\), duality gives
\[
 H_2(U_j,\partial U_j)=H^4(U_j),
\]
and this is free. The free ranks are d at the cusp, \(\rho_j(d)\)
at a zero-Chern additive original, \(s_j\) at a nonzero-Chern
additive original, \(\nu_j\) at a nonzero-Chern multiplicative
original, and the component count at a rank-one filling.
The circle-bundle Gysin and component-orbit bases above compute these groups. For example a nonzero additive
original has \(H_3\) of its angular circle bundle equal to
\(H_2(N)=\mathbb Z^{s_j}\); product with the suspension circle
therefore has \(H^4=\mathbb Z^{s_j}\). The multiplicative case
gives \(\mathbb Z^{\nu_j}\) by the same map.

Choose the dual normal discs at the generic points of these
component cycles. In a component of multiplicity \(m_C\), the
base parameter has the form \(q=u^{m_C}\) times a nonvanishing
unit. A disc in a nonzero line frame lifts to the prequotient
line space and has \(\gamma\) displacement zero. Its boundary is
therefore \(m_Cx_j\) plus a vertical class, which vanishes
in \(H_1(E)\). The cusp and primitive Mumford discs have \(m_C=1\).
For a component orbit choose any representative; the quotient
is a local biholomorphism there, so this disc intersects the
orbit cycle once. Its coefficient remains \(m_C\).
Every original has a multiplicity-one outer component, so the
images at site j generate exactly \(\mathbb Zx_j\) in \(H_1(E)\).

The complete degree-three images are the full boundary kernels
proved above. Passing through \(H_2(E)\) gives the exact sequence
\[
 0\longrightarrow C_d\longrightarrow H_2(X)
 \longrightarrow
 \ker\!\left\{\bigoplus_jH^4(U_j)\longrightarrow H_1(E)\right\}
 \longrightarrow0,\qquad C_d=\operatorname{coker}B .
\tag{D.WP11}\hypertarget{tag-027Q}{}\label{maps:eq:D.WP11}
\]

An explicit kernel algorithm retains \(H_1(E)\)'s torsion: if P is its
integer power-relation matrix in the omitted-edge coordinates and
M the displayed component-disc
boundary matrix, solve \(Mz=Pz'\) over the integers. Project the
integer kernel of \([M,-P]\) to z. The columns of P are independent
by their base coordinates, so this projection is injective on the
relation coefficients and gives exactly the required subgroup of
the component lattice. Hermite or reversible Smith operations
supply a basis and its inverse coordinates.

For each such basis vector choose its relative disc chain. Its
boundary bounds the combination of the power discs specified by
z' and an integral chain in E. Gluing these chains produces a
closed two-cycle with that relative coordinate. Subtracting these
cycles and reading the remaining exterior coordinate gives an
inverse to the splitting of the exact sequence.

Denote the component-disc boundary map by \(\Gamma\). Its rank is
\(s_{\mathrm{unf}}-r\), because its cokernel is \(H_1(X)\) and \(H_1(E)\)
has rank \(s_{\mathrm{unf}}\). Its domain has rank
\(d+(s_{\mathrm{unf}}-1)+\beta+L\). Thus its kernel is free of rank
\[
 \operatorname{rank}\ker\Gamma=d-1+\beta+L+r.
\tag{D.WP12}\hypertarget{tag-027R}{}\label{maps:eq:D.WP12}
\]
The integral basis includes every torsion-index effect.
The exact sequence and the integral section constructed above give
\[
              H_2(X)=C_d\oplus\mathbb Z^{d-1+\beta+L+r}.
\]
Its inverse reads the relative component coordinates and then the
remaining exterior class modulo B.

\emph{The full group, the unrestricted ranks, and every homology group.}

\emph{The nonabelian vertical quotient.}

The cusp kills its primitive short lattice
\(S=\mathbb Z\langle u,\delta\rangle\) and the origin-disc
meridian. Its normal closure under the base peripheral
conjugations is the same vertical subgroup for all d:
on vectors of \(\gamma\) coordinate zero, \eqref{maps:eq:D.WP2} is literally
the original matrix. The vector \(u\) and its conjugates
therefore give the same integer vanishing words as in
\ref{maps:src:D.2.23}.

On 170 rows those words give two elliptic vectors u,v
of determinant one after subtracting their angular
coordinates. If \(u=(u_1,u_2),v=(v_1,v_2)\), their exact
inverse is
\[
 e_1=v_2\widetilde u-u_2\widetilde v,\qquad
 e_2=-v_1\widetilde u+u_1\widetilde v .
\]
Together with \(\delta\) this kills ker \(\chi\).

The two OS46/II rows have \((a,b)=(1,4),(4,1)\).
Their first short vectors are \(u=(1,1),v=(-4,-1)\),
giving \(3e_1=-\widetilde u-\widetilde v\) and the
index-three elliptic sublattice \(x-y=0\bmod3\).
Their \(I_3^*\) is kept original in both scope readings.

For \(a=1\) its line Chern vector evaluates to one on
the sphere met by P. The circle-bundle Hopf disc
therefore kills \(\delta\) and the simply connected affine
\(D_7\) plumbing contracts the elliptic loops by projection
and path lifting. In particular the boundary
loop \(w_1=2e_1+\delta\) bounds. Subtracting
\(w_1-\delta=2e_1\) from \(3e_1\) gives \(e_1\).

For \(a=4\) the line is trivial over that same plumbing.
Its boundary-to-cover map on the first three coordinates
is
\[
                   (x,y,z)\longmapsto z-2x-y,
\]
with section \(k\mapsto k\delta\). It kills
\(w_4=e_1+2\delta\), so \(e_1\) again bounds. Then
\(e_2=\widetilde u-e_1\). These are unchanged maps on the
line bundle for every permitted d; only the
suspension arrow has been iterated. The original star cap therefore kills the remaining index-three quotient.

Every vanishing relation used has \(\chi\) value zero.
The unrolled contraction defines a return map
on every cap, with \(\gamma\) mapped to one. This proves
the reverse inclusion of the normal subgroup. Thus
the global vertical quotient is exactly
\[
 \Lambda/\mathcal N\longleftrightarrow\mathbb Z\gamma,
 \qquad [v]\longmapsto\chi(v)\gamma,\quad
       k\gamma\longmapsto[k\gamma].
\]
The two compositions are the identity.

\emph{Every order, numerator and clutch.}

A boundary fibre generates the original or Mumford
cover cap group: move a loop off the central divisor,
then contract its meridian using a transverse disc
at a multiplicity-one point in an extending line
frame. The toric coordinate quotient gives the same
surjection for a Mumford model. After the vertical quotient, the
cover cap group is \(\mathbb Z\gamma\), with return
as forward map and \(\gamma\) as inverse section.

At a free logarithm, select a root over the boundary
basepoint. Its fibre maps isomorphically to the quotient
fibre, with inverse choosing that root representative.
The deck path \(c_i\) has the \(m_i\)-fold power \(v_i\).
Conjugation is \(A_i(d)\), and \(\chi A_i(d)=\chi\). The full
reduced local group is therefore
\[
 \langle\gamma,c_i\mid[\gamma,c_i]=1,\
                      c_i^{m_i}=\gamma^{\mu_i}\rangle,
             \qquad \mu_i=\chi(v_i).
\]
The inverse normal form reads the covering-sheet index
\(0\le j<m_i\), then the remaining return exponent r,
and writes \(\gamma^r c_i^j\). The injection of the
cover return group proves uniqueness.

Before taking the contraction quotient choose the
peripheral lifts closed in its infinite cyclic cover.
Their product has return zero, as do all line-frame
windings. Thus the initial canonical clutch is zero.
The order-one map of the regular and clutch construction realizes every integer e.

Van Kampen and the exact inverse maps above now give
the full group
\[
 \pi_1(X)=\left\langle\gamma,c_1,\ldots,c_s\ \middle|\
 [\gamma,c_i]=1,\ c_i^{m_i}=\gamma^{\mu_i},\
                  c_1\cdots c_s=\gamma^e\right\rangle.
\]
Its inverse map sends each fibre vector to its \(\chi\)
power of \(\gamma\), each unchanged meridian to one, and
each deck path to \(c_i\). The displayed relations
are exactly their monodromy, vanishing, power and
global product relations, so both compositions fix
every generator.

A finite lift change by \(\lambda\) has
\(\mu_i'=\mu_i+\chi(N_{m_i}\lambda)
        =\mu_i+m_i\chi(\lambda)\).
The global clutch changes by the sum of \(\chi(\lambda)\).
These are the generator changes
\(c'_i=c_i\gamma^{\chi(\lambda)}\), with inverse
\(c_i=c'_i\gamma^{-\chi(\lambda)}\).
They also match the normal-sweep maps in the regular and clutch construction.

The abelianization matrix, on \(\gamma\),\(c_1\),\ldots,\(c_s\), has
rows
\[
 (-\mu_i,0,\ldots,m_i,\ldots,0),\qquad(-e,1,\ldots,1).
\]
Its Smith maps give \(H_1=\mathbb Z^r\oplus A_1\) and
inverse coordinates. Over the rationals the first s
rows eliminate \(c_i\) as \((\mu_i/m_i)\gamma\), so
\[
 r=1\quad\text{exactly when}\quad
       e-\sum_i\mu_i/m_i=0;
 \qquad r=0\text{ otherwise}.
\]
This statement also covers an empty site set and
order-one sites through the same matrix and its
elimination. The same eliminations apply to every finite number of sites and every positive order.

\emph{The free rank of the full boundary cokernel.}

Over \(\mathbb Q\), the literal map \(S_d\) identifies
the graph complex and fixed-peripheral insertions with
their weight-one counterparts. More explicitly,
\[
 [A_i(d)-I]\operatorname{diag}(S_d^{-1},\ldots,S_d^{-1})
        =S_d^{-1}[A_i-I],
\]
and \(J_i(d)S_d^{-1}\lambda\) is the blockwise inverse
\(S_d\) image of \(J_i(1)\lambda\). The full fixed-normal
map at weight one is onto the graph kernel and has
exactly the one \(\delta\) relation, by the integral map and inverse of \ref{maps:src:D.2.31}. These displayed rational
maps prove the corresponding rank and relation
for every d.~Each added identity site adds its full
four-dimensional fixed space, with the same one
\(\delta\) relation and the deletion/restoration inverse.

At a logarithmic site the full norm is m times the
fixed-plane projection. For a fixed u, \eqref{maps:eq:D.WP6} therefore
gives over the rationals
\[
                    t_i(u)=\omega_d(u,v_i)s/m_i.
\]
The root column is redundant there because
\(\omega_d(v_i,v_i)=0\). At every unchanged cap the
fixed sweeps are zero. After deleting the dummy clutch
site, the one \(\delta\) relation consequently becomes
\[
        db\left(e-\sum_i\mu_i/m_i\right)s=0.
\]
Every other graph coordinate has been eliminated by
the explicit fixed-normal maps. If \(L=0\), the Euler criterion and scalar graph relation
give \(\operatorname{rank}C_d=r\).
If \(L>0\), one of the positive coefficients \(dh_i\) kills
s over the rationals, and \(\operatorname{rank}C_d=0\).
This rational calculation is used only for the free
rank; all torsion remains the integral Smith group
of B already constructed.

Substituting these ranks in \eqref{maps:eq:D.WP11}--\eqref{maps:eq:D.WP12} proves
\[
 b_2=
 \begin{cases}
 d-1+\beta+2r,&L=0,\\
 d-1+\beta+L+r,&L>0.
 \end{cases}
\]

\emph{Euler characteristic and integral duality.}

The smooth torus bundle exterior has Euler characteristic
zero. Every noncusp original is a circle mapping-torus
construction and has Euler characteristic zero; the
finite and regular cores are free torus quotients and
also have Euler characteristic zero. Their boundary
mapping tori have Euler characteristic zero. The cusp homology gives \(\chi(N_d)=2d\). Additivity on these pieces therefore proves \(\chi(X)=2d\).

The closed complex threefold is oriented. Integral
Poincaré duality and UCT give the free symmetry
\(b_5=b_1=r,\ b_4=b_2\), torsion in \(H_4\) equal to \(A_1\),
and torsion in \(H_3\) equal to T. More explicitly, a Smith
torsion generator of order n determines the character
\(j\mapsto j/n\) in \(\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z\); its
Bockstein followed by cap product with the fundamental
class gives the dual torsion coordinate. Evaluating
its linking character on the same generator is the
inverse. Free coordinates use dual integral cocycles
and the same cap product. Thus the identifications
give the integral dual groups and their inverse coordinates.

The Euler identity
\(2-2r+2b_2-b_3=2d\) now gives
\[
 b_3=
 \begin{cases}
 2\beta+2r,&L=0,\\
 2\beta+2L,&L>0.
 \end{cases}
\]
The complete groups are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
 j&H_j(X;\mathbb Z)\\ \hline
 0,6&\mathbb Z\\
 1&\mathbb Z^r\oplus A_1\\
 2&\mathbb Z^{b_2}\oplus T\\
 3&\mathbb Z^{b_3}\oplus T\\
 4&\mathbb Z^{b_2}\oplus A_1\\
 5&\mathbb Z^r .
\end{array}
\]
This proves the displayed homology groups for every allowed parameter.

At \(d=1\) the covering \(p_d\) is the
identity, and every map above restricts to its weight-one counterpart. This includes the ordinary
identity on the subgroup lattice and the empty
zero-sum component lattice in the displayed cusp-relative decomposition.

\emph{Enumeration and the two starred-cap scopes.}

Let \(\mathcal P\) use all five finite-good types II, III, IV,
\(\mathrm{III}^*\), \(\mathrm{IV}^*\), each with original O or free finite F, and retain
every odd \(I_n^*\) original. At each nonzero-Chern zero-free
multiplicative site take original O or primitive Mumford M.
At each zero-Chern multiplicative site identify O and M through
the marked boundary maps of the zero-Chern multiplicative construction; use M as its
representative. Use C at the selected weighted cusp.

Let \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{all\ star\ O}}\) be the subset with
O at \(\mathrm{III}^*\) and \(\mathrm{IV}^*\) as well. Its inclusion j keeps every site
label. The projection \(\pi\) from \(\mathcal P\) replaces each
\(\mathrm{III}^*\)/\(\mathrm{IV}^*\) F by O and keeps every other label. Thus
\(\pi j=I\), with all the changed local labels explicit.
This is a map of the finite pattern sets. The local kernel
change made by \(\pi\) is the change from \eqref{maps:eq:D.WP6} to
\eqref{maps:eq:D.WP7} or the three additive kernel columns, already described by those formulas.

The quotient from all individual multiplicative choices
to these patterns forgets O versus M exactly at the
zero-Chern multiplicative sites. Its canonical section
chooses M there. The full inverse fibre of a pattern is
the independent set of its \(2^{z}\) O/M choices, where z
is the number of those sites. The zero-Chern multiplicative construction gives the
marked integral kernel morphisms between these choices.

At a nonzero-Chern multiplicative site, the primitive
class \(k_d\) is killed by the original cap and maps to a
primitive nonzero class in the Mumford cap. Its
\(\omega_d\) value is \(-db/\nu\ne0\), so their marked
kernels differ. At an additive site the original
contains all fixed-normal sweeps in its kernel.
For the finite alternative the rational kernel graph
is \(t(u)=\omega_d(u,v)s/m\). The fixed-plane form
is nondegenerate, since
\(\omega_d(\delta,\ell_d)=-db\,g_0\ne0\), and a free
affine power v cannot be zero. Hence some fixed sweep
has nonzero transfer. The finite kernel has no rational
pure fibre element, since its normal projection is an
isomorphism onto the fixed plane. This proves that it
differs from the original kernel. Thus the stated
identifications are exactly the local marked-kernel
identifications used in the enumeration.

For each defining profile the finite factor enumeration given by the component-degree equation
is exhaustive: a ranges through the positive divisors
of \(d_0/n_*\), which is at most 30 in the defining profile data. For each resulting row take the Cartesian product
of the site option sets just stated. Its inverse reads
the original row and every site option. This proves
completeness and absence of duplicate marked choices
by the displayed inverse.

The finite factor and site-option enumeration gives the following totals.
Here R is the natural-row count, K the nonzero-Chern
multiplicative position count, P the broad pattern
count, S the all-star-original subset, and A the
individual original/Mumford choices.

by tubing two positive parallel copies of $S^2$ in $S^2\times S^4$.

with $H_2=\mathbb Z/p\langle e_p\rangle$, $b_3=0$,

\[
 H_2(X)=\mathbb Z/(2p)\langle s\rangle,\quad H_3(X)=\mathbb Z/(2p),\quad b_3(X)=0,
 \qquad

 \quad\hbox{orientation-preservingly}.
 \tag{D.MP1}\hypertarget{tag-0209}{}\label{maps:eq:D.MP1}

$\mu(X)=pt\,\gamma_3(s)$. The generator $\gamma_3(s)$ is the
reduced positive complex $\mathbb{CP}^3$ class. Set
$\epsilon=0$ for $P_p=0$ and $\epsilon=1$ otherwise.

complete table, where $\mu_{2p}$ is the coefficient of $\gamma_3(s)$, is

origin frame, have the stated inverse matrices and ordered product
identity. Thus they define one line on the actual exterior $V$.

sweep is zero: on $x=t u$, $\Omega(u,u)=0$, and the scalar-one

\[

Here are the maps identifying this line with the actual holomorphic

logarithm of $G$. The theta ratio
$\vartheta(z-a\zeta_G)/\vartheta(z)$, with reciprocal inverse,
identifies the actual divisor line $\mathcal O(aG-O)$ with its

\[

\]

For the complete integral class, the order-two calculation in
\ref{maps:src:D.2.35} gives $H_6(K(\mathbb Z/2,2);\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z/2$
with generator the reduced positive complex $\mathbb{CP}^3$ and
detector its mod-two cube. For $p=5,7$, \ref{maps:src:D.1.10}
gives the corresponding cyclic group and cube detector.
The full coprime homotopy maps of item~13 then give, with
$s=1\in\mathbb Z/(2p)$,

\[
 H_6(K(\mathbb Z/(2p),2);\mathbb Z)
        =\mathbb Z/(2p)\langle\gamma_3(s)\rangle .    \qquad\textup{(60)}
\]

The positive generator is the image of the complex-oriented
$\mathbb{CP}^3$ under integer reduction. Its two primary projections
are the generators just specified. Thus the pair of ordinary cube
evaluations detects the complete integral group; the inverse maps
are explicit below. The projections to $\mathbb Z/2$ and
$\mathbb Z/p$ send $s\mapsto1$, and send $\gamma_3(s)\mapsto \gamma_3(1)$. Their inverse on homology uses the inclusions

\[
 e_2\mapsto p s,\qquad e_p\mapsto(1-p)s,\quad
 \gamma_3(e_2)\mapsto p^3\gamma_3(s)=p\gamma_3(s),
 \quad\gamma_3(e_p)\mapsto(1-p)^3\gamma_3(s)
                               =(1-p)\gamma_3(s).   \qquad\textup{(61)}
\]

These are integer Chinese-remainder maps with inverse reduction in
the two factors; the coefficients are idempotent modulo $2p$.
Equations \eqref{maps:eq:D.MP7}--(59) consequently give the full invariant

\[
               \mu(X)=p(1+\kappa\bmod2)\gamma_3(s). \qquad\textup{(62)}
\]

No coordinate has been lost by reducing only modulo $p$.

\item \emph{The refined Pontryagin class and exact Tate conversion.}

On a fixed curve for $C_p$, let the ordinary normal roots be
$x_1,x_2$. They and the tangent root are curve classes. The equivariant
normal roots are $x_1+\lambda t,x_2-\lambda t$, and

\[
 p_1(TX)|F=-2e_F.                                    \qquad\textup{(63)}
\]

Indeed $x_1^2=x_2^2=x_1x_2=c_1(TF)^2=0$ on a curve; expanding
both sides gives $2\lambda^2t^2+2\lambda t(x_1-x_2)$.
The identity allows unequal ordinary normal degrees. Hence the exact
localized pairing is

\[
 \langle\alpha_p\,\rho_p p_1(TX),[X]_p\rangle
    =-2\left(a(\nu-b\kappa)-{b\over p}\right)
    =2\left({b\over p}-a\nu\right)\pmod p.          \qquad\textup{(64)}
\]

The degree-one mixed term from $E_p$ integrates to zero. Naturality
of the refined invariant under reduction to $\mathbb Z/p$, followed
by the quarter map of \ref{maps:src:D.1.11} and the Bezout inverse of four modulo $p$,
gives

\[
            P_p={b/p-a\nu\over2}\in\mathbb F_p.     \qquad\textup{(65)}
\]

The action conversion retains every generator. In the genuine Tate
marking at the unique $I_p$, $r=-\kappa_i$ and $w=(ar)^{-1}$.
The zero-degree equivariant integration of $U_p$ gives

\[
 {a\nu\over\nu^2}-{b/p\over w^2}=0,
 \quad w^2={\nu(b/p)\over a},\quad
 P_p={b/p\over2}\left(1-{\nu^2\over w^2}\right).    \qquad\textup{(66)}
\]

All denominators are units in these rows. The subgroup automorphism
$z\mapsto z^{\nu^{-1}}$, with inverse $z\mapsto z^\nu$, changes
both normal pairs: cusp to $(-1,1)$, elliptic to
$(w/\nu,-w/\nu)$. The Borel character and degree-one generator
are both pulled back by the same exponent. Thus (65)--(66) use one
action on the actual common space. The zero criterion is
$w^2=\nu^2$, not a rescaling that changes only one component.


For comparison with the marking that evaluates to one on $C_f$, put
$z=(a\nu)^{-1}\alpha_p$. Its homology generator is $g_z=(a\nu)s$,
with inverse coordinate evaluation by $z$. The simultaneous action
conversion gives
\[
 z[E_p]=-\frac{w^2}{\nu^2},\qquad
 \langle z^3,[X]_p\rangle=0,\qquad
 \langle z\,\rho_p p_1,[X]_p\rangle
       =-2\left(1-\frac{w^2}{\nu^2}\right).
\tag{D.MP8}\hypertarget{tag-020H}{}\label{maps:eq:D.MP8}
\]
The corresponding refined coefficient is $(w^2/\nu^2-1)/2$.
Multiplication by $a\nu$, with inverse $(a\nu)^{-1}$, recovers
the primitive coefficient $P_p$. The physical weights are $w=4$
at the order-five rows with $a=1$, $w=3$ there when $a=3$, and
$w=4$ at every order-seven row. The selected $\nu$ is three
on $56(1,10)$ and $56/II(1,10)$, and one on the other rows.
Thus the common normalized weights $w/\nu$ are three in all
nonzero order-five cases and four in its zero case. This accounts
for every assignment in \eqref{maps:eq:D.MP2}.

For the two-primary coordinate, use the precise primary quotient on
\cite[Sections~3.7 and~3.12, pp.~803, 807]{manZhubr75}:

\[
 \Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_6(K(\mathbb Z/2,2))
   =\mathbb Z\langle\epsilon,\zeta\rangle/
                        \langle\epsilon,2\zeta\rangle,
       \quad P(\zeta)=1,\quad h(\zeta)=\gamma_3(1).   \qquad\textup{(67)}
\]

The quotient sends $(A,B)\mapsto B\bmod2$; its inverse chooses the
reduction of $\zeta=[\mathbb CP^3\to\mathbb CP^\infty]$.
Its cubic is one. Therefore the marked classifying map
$X\to K(\mathbb Z/2,2)$ has refined coefficient exactly \eqref{maps:eq:D.MP7}.
The map $P$ is natural, so this is the actual mod-two projection
of $\mathfrak p(X)$. No division by four in $\mathbb Z/(2p)$
is used.

Set $t=1+\kappa\pmod2$. The unique coefficient $P_{2p}$ is
specified by

\[
        P_{2p}\equiv t\pmod2,\qquad
        P_{2p}\equiv P_p\pmod p.                    \qquad\textup{(68)}
\]

The inverse CRT map is $ (t,P_p)\mapsto p t+(1-p)P_p\pmod{2p}$.
Its composites are identity on both coordinates. This proves the
full marked data in the theorem:

\[
 (H_2,b_3,\mathfrak p,\mu)
  =\left(\mathbb Z/(2p),0,P_{2p}s,p t\gamma_3(s)\right).
                                                               \qquad\textup{(69)}
\]

\item \emph{Exact connected-sum marking and oriented classification.}

The construction of $M_0$ in \ref{maps:src:D.2.35} uses an oriented sphere representing
$2[S^2]$ in $S^2\times S^4$. Its normal bundle is trivial because
its oriented rank-four clutching has zero $w_2$; the framing class is
unique since $\pi_2(SO(4))=0$. Its index-three surgery trace sends
the incoming positive generator to the order-two generator and the
outgoing second homology isomorphically onto it. The common mod-two
class has incoming square zero, so its cube on $M_0$ is zero.
The conic trace has the same marked maps starting from CP3 and the
incoming hyperplane cube one. Both traces extend the spin structures.
Their exact kernel/cokernel maps, with inverse sections, are the integral surgery-trace maps of \ref{maps:src:D.2.35}. The quotient (67) then gives all invariants in
(1), including the refined coordinate at the even order.

The oriented connected sum $M_t\# Z_{p,\epsilon}$ is simply connected,
spin and has $b_3=0$, with

\[
 H_2=\mathbb Z/2\langle e_2\rangle\oplus
                  \mathbb Z/p\langle e_p\rangle,
 \quad\mathfrak p=t e_2+\epsilon e_p,
 \quad\mu=t\gamma_3(e_2).                            \qquad\textup{(70)}
\]

These are the actual addition maps: puncture both manifolds in discs
where their classifying maps are constant, attach the oriented neck,
and use the bordism with one one-handle from the disjoint union to
the connected sum. The classifying map extends by the constant map
on that handle. Its boundary fundamental classes add and $P$ is a
bordism homomorphism. The homology inclusions of the summands and
collapse to them are inverse coordinates. The finite cross terms
between the two torsion factors vanish by the integer Kunneth maps,
whose tensor and Tor groups have coprime orders. This is also the
same exact CRT equivalence of the two Eilenberg--Mac Lane markings
used in (61).

Here is the marking that compares (70) to (69). If $P_p\ne0$, put

\[
 k=P_{2p}-tp\pmod{2p},\quad
 \Phi(e_2)=p s,\quad\Phi(e_p)=k s,
 \quad\Phi^{-1}(n s)=(n\bmod2)e_2+
                       (P_p^{-1}n\bmod p)e_p.        \qquad\textup{(71)}
\]

Then $k$ is even and $k\bmod p=P_p\ne0$, so it has order $p$.
Both compositions in (71) are identity. Moreover

\[
 \Phi(t e_2+e_p)=P_{2p}s,\quad
 K(\Phi,2)_*(t\gamma_3(e_2))=tp^3\gamma_3(s)
                                        =tp\gamma_3(s).        \qquad\textup{(72)}
\]

If $P_p=0$, take $\Phi(e_p)=(1-p)s$ and replace $P_p^{-1}$
in the inverse by one. Then $P_{2p}=tp\pmod{2p}$, and the same
identities hold with $\epsilon=0$. These give every generator
rescaling and its inverse. The concrete maps in the table are
$(e_2,e_p)\mapsto(5s,2s)$ for the nonzero order-five cases,
$(5s,6s)$ for its zero case, and $(7s,4s)$ for order seven.
Their inverse odd coefficients are respectively three, one and two.

Use the marked recognition theorem. Theorem~5 of \cite[p.~796]{manZhubr75} gives the injection

\[
 (P,h):\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_6(K(G,2))
                    \longrightarrow G\oplus H_6(K(G,2);\mathbb Z).
\]

The construction in \cite[Theorem~3, p.~795; Section~4.1, p.~809]{manZhubr75} preserves the
specified $H_2\cong G$, kills the free part of $H_3$, and its
marked uniqueness proof yields a degree-positive diffeomorphism from
equality of the resulting bordism classes. Here both free ranks vanish, and both manifolds
have the unique spin structure required. By (69)--(72), their marked
$(P,h)$ agree. Injection and marked uniqueness give the oriented
diffeomorphism in \eqref{maps:eq:D.MP1}, inducing precisely $\Phi$ on second homology.
Its inverse induces (71)'s inverse. Thus the connected-sum conclusion
is an actual oriented identification with its prescribed homology map.

Every type listed in \eqref{maps:eq:D.MP2} is realized.
For a row without a finite cap choose $e=1$. At a finite cap choose
$m=d_i$, $e=1$, $n=m-1$, $r=0$, and the affine vector $v/m$.
It is free, has $me-n=1$, and is an actual allowed construction.
Equations (23)--(69) prove the same result for every other allowed
finite multiplicity, numerator, residue and affine vector.

Finally, an automorphism of $\mathbb Z/(2p)$ is multiplication by a
unit $u$. It sends $P_{2p}$ to $uP_{2p}$ and the full $\mu$
coefficient to $u^3\mu_{2p}$. Modulo two, $u=1$, so $t$ is
preserved. Modulo $p$, a unit preserves zero versus nonzero. These
two properties distinguish the five listed types. Conversely, any
two rows with the same pair $(t,\epsilon)$ are related by the unit
$u\equiv1\pmod2$, $u\equiv P_p'/P_p\pmod p$ when $P_p\ne0$,
or by one on the odd factor when both are zero. Its inverse is the
corresponding inverse unit, and it preserves the full $(P,\mu)$.
The same marked recognition gives their oriented diffeomorphism.
This proves exactly three and two types, with the counts in \eqref{maps:eq:D.MP2}.


\item \emph{The full coprime homotopy and bordism maps.}
Put $K_q=K(\mathbb Z/q,2)$ for $q=2,p$. The cyclic-group
resolution makes the positive homology of $K(\mathbb Z/q,1)$
zero over $\mathbb Z[1/q]$. The path-loop Serre sequence, whose
total space is contractible, then makes the positive homology
of $K_q$ zero over that ring. Exactness of localization implies
that each positive integral homology element is killed by a
power of $q$. For elements of the two factors, a Bezout identity
between their annihilating powers makes their tensor zero.
Likewise $\operatorname{Tor}(\mathbb Z/2^a,B)=B[2^a]=0$ for
$p$-primary $B$; finite direct sums and filtered colimits give
the assertion for all the positive homology groups.

The reduced integral Kunneth sequence therefore makes
$K_2\wedge K_p$ acyclic. The based CW inclusion
\[
 i:K_2\vee K_p\longrightarrow K_2\times K_p
\tag{D.MP9}\hypertarget{tag-020I}{}\label{maps:eq:D.MP9}
\]
is an integral homology equivalence of simply connected spaces.
Every relative homotopy group vanishes: a first nonzero one
would be the corresponding zero relative homology group by
relative Hurewicz. The inverse can be constructed on cells.
Start with the identity of the wedge; injectivity on homotopy
groups extends its retraction across each attaching cell, and
surjectivity adjusts that extension so that its composite with
$i$ is homotopic to the original cell map relative to its
boundary. The homotopy-extension property assembles the choices
over successive skeleta. This gives a based map $q$ with
$qi=\mathrm{id}$ and $iq\simeq\mathrm{id}$ relative to the wedge.
Thus \eqref{maps:eq:D.MP9} is a full CW homotopy equivalence,
with the stated inverse at that homotopy scope. The coefficient maps
below may be implemented by the Eilenberg--Mac Lane functor on
degree-two chain complexes in simplicial abelian groups; in that
model their two composites are literally the identity.

The coefficient maps
\[
 \theta(n)=(n\bmod2,n\bmod p),\qquad
 \theta^{-1}(x,y)=px+(1-p)y\pmod{2p}
\]
are exact inverses. Apply the Eilenberg--Mac Lane construction
to these degree-two coefficient maps and then use $i,q$.
The finite wedge axiom for the spin-bordism Thom spectrum gives
\[
 \Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_6(K(\mathbb Z/(2p),2))
  \cong
 \Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_6(K_2)\oplus
 \Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_6(K_p).
\tag{D.MP10}\hypertarget{tag-020A}{}\label{maps:eq:D.MP10}
\]
Here $\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_6(\mathrm{pt})=0$, also a consequence
of the injective pair $(P,h)$ for coefficient group zero.
The forward map in \eqref{maps:eq:D.MP10} is the pair of
coefficient projections. Its inverse is the sum of the two
factor inclusions followed by $K(\theta^{-1},2)_*$.
An automorphism on the odd factor, multiplication by $r$, lifts
to the unit $p+(1-p)r$ modulo $2p$; its inverse is
$p+(1-p)r^{-1}$.

For the connected sum, contract the classifying maps on the
removed balls and collapse its neck to the common basepoint.
The inclusions and summand collapse maps give inverse homology
coordinates. The oriented spin one-handle bordism extends those
constant maps and adds the two bordism classes. Composing with
the explicit marking already given in (71)--(72) produces the
same pair as $X$. Thus the two-primary value, every odd-primary
coefficient and every possible mixed bordism coordinate have
been determined under the actual maps and their inverses.

\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}
\begin{enumerate}[label={$\langle1\rangle$\arabic*.},leftmargin=*]
\item \emph{1. The invariant which must be computed.}
We first identify its complete target from the primary classification
and the actual Pontryagin operation. Zhubr's epimorphism in Section~3.11
and his free calculation in Section~3.12 show that
$\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_6(K(\mathbb Z/3,2))$ is generated by the
images of $\epsilon,\zeta$, where
\[
 (P,h)(\epsilon)=(6,0),\qquad
 \zeta=[\mathbb {CP}^3,\text{hyperplane}].
\]
The image of $\epsilon$ has both invariants zero: its first is six
modulo three, and its second is the image of zero. The injectivity
in Zhubr's Theorem~5 therefore kills that image.
Lemma~3.14 gives $N(\mathbb Z/3)=0$, so the fundamental-class map
identifies this cyclic bordism group with
$H_6(K(\mathbb Z/3,2);\mathbb Z)$; the mod-two obstruction target
is zero because all positive homology is three-primary.
These facts use \cite[Sections 3.11--3.14 and Theorem 5]{manZhubr75}.

\item The cyclic generator has order dividing nine. On
$\mathbb {CP}^1\times\mathbb {CP}^2$ take the integral class
$3x+y$, with $x,y$ the two hyperplane classes. Its mod-three
reduction factors through $\mathbb {CP}^2$, and hence sends the
six-dimensional fundamental class to zero. Before reduction its
cube evaluates to nine. Naturality therefore gives nine times the
universal generator equal to zero.
For the opposite bound, Thomas's Pontryagin third power is a natural
operation
\[
 \mathcal P_3:H^2(-;\mathbb Z/3)\longrightarrow
                              H^6(-;\mathbb Z/9).
\]
Its value on the reduced hyperplane class of $\mathbb {CP}^3$
evaluates to a generator of $\mathbb Z/9$
\cite[equation (2.8), p.267]{ffThomas56}. Thus the cyclic group has
order exactly nine. Evaluation of $\mathcal P_3$ detects its entire
generator, and hence the whole fundamental-class invariant. This is
stronger than evaluating the ordinary cube modulo three.

\item \emph{2. The common-piece comparison and its circle geometry.}
\ref{maps:src:D.2.26} gives $H_2(X)=H_3(X)=\mathbb Z/3$ and $b_3=0$ for every
simply connected member in \eqref{maps:eq:D.T31}. In particular $H^2(X;\mathbb Z)=0$,
so $c_1(X)=0$ and $X$ is spin. Let
$u\in H^2(X;\mathbb F_3)$ be the generator normalized below.
All the geometric hypotheses of the doubled-line calculation in
\ref{maps:src:D.2.36} hold here. We record the exact inputs to ensure that no
prime-greater-than-three conclusion is being imported.

\item Remove the additive caps and one ordinary clutch disc to form $W$.
In all seven marked initial rows the actual multiplicative angular
columns generate $\ker\gamma^*$ with three unit Smith factors.
Consequently $\pi_1(W)=\mathbb Z_\gamma\times F_r$ is torsion-free.
The integral degree-one bridge calculation and surjective degree-two
cap boundary maps give $H_2(V)\twoheadrightarrow H_2(W)$, as in
\eqref{maps:eq:D.C26}. The pure fibre functional is
$\Omega=a\,u_1^*u_2^*+b\,\gamma^*\delta^*$, with $3\mid b$
and $3\nmid a$. Its finite normal coefficients are divisible by
$b/q_i=3$, its original additive coefficients are zero, and the
ordinary clutch coefficient is $be$. Thus its mod-three reduction
is the actual global degree-two generator, with zero marked swept
values. The doubled factors \eqref{maps:eq:D.OP4} and the exact integral supports
\eqref{maps:eq:D.OP5}, \eqref{maps:eq:D.OP5a} produce the corresponding line on $W$.

\item The scalar circle has precisely two strata whose stabilizer order is
divisible by three: the rational curve $C$ fixed by the whole circle,
and one elliptic double curve $E$ with stabilizer exactly $C_3$.
The latter is at the unique $I_3$ position. On its complement all
stabilizers are finite of order prime to three. This includes the
finite logarithmic caps: primitivity of their actual gamma numerators
makes the scalar circle free there, for every allowed order.
The original additive caps have free scalar action as well.
The seven exact Tate markings in the certificate verify the remaining
multiplicative assertions, including the primitive short period
$(3,aj)$ at $E$ and the two normal characters
$w,-w$, where $w=(aj)^{-1}=\pm1$ in $\mathbb F_3$.

\item The doubled auxiliary line has zero $C_3$ character at both $C$ and
$E$. Its degree on $C$ is a unit modulo three. Normalize $u$ by
$\langle u,[C]\rangle=1$. The torsion-free group of $W$ gives the
same simultaneous fixed-point comparison as in D.2.36: once an
equivariant lift has zero point character on $C$, it also has zero
point character on $E$. Indeed the two fixed-point copies of $BC_3$
represent the same order-three subgroup in
$\pi_1(W_{C_3})=\pi_1(W)\times C_3$. The group-cohomology difference
from half the auxiliary-line class has a common degree-two base
coefficient; the possible mixed degree-one term does not change
that coefficient. This comparison uses the complete normal columns,
including arbitrary finite twists.

\item \emph{3. The full-circle lift and the elliptic Borel space.}
The generator $u$ admits a lift
\[
                 \widehat u\in H^2_{S^1}(X;\mathbb F_3).
\]
In the Borel spectral sequence the only possible differentials out
of ordinary degree two have targets involving $H^1(X;\mathbb F_3)$
or $H^3(BS^1;\mathbb F_3)$; both are zero. Adding a multiple of the
base generator normalizes its restriction on the fixed curve to
\[

circle is trivial, so equivariantly $E$ is the product of a free
$S^1/C_3$ orbit and a circle. Therefore
\[

\]
where $\eta\in H^1(BC_3;\mathbb F_3)$ and

factor. Formula \eqref{maps:eq:D.T35} retains the possible nonzero mixed class;
it does not assert that $u$ descends to the coarse quotient $X/C_3$.
In fact the mixed term is generally essential.

and vanishing on odd-dimensional classes, and independently proves
vanishing on suspensions

\[

                       \quad\text{in }H^6(E_{S^1};\mathbb Z/9).

\]

from the two-dimensional curve, whose degree-six cohomology is zero.

suspended classes are irrelevant here; the cited formulas explicitly

\item \emph{4. Why the full order-nine class vanishes globally.}
Put $R=\mathbb Z/9$. Choose disjoint invariant tubular neighborhoods
$N$ of $C\sqcup E$ and let $Y=X\setminus\operatorname{int}N$.

to three. The quotient $Y/S^1$ is a compact five-dimensional orbifold
with boundary. The Borel projection to this quotient, for both $Y$
and its boundary, has local cohomology fibres $BH$ with $H$ finite
of order invertible in $R$. Finite averaging gives
$H^q(BH;R)=0$ for $q>0$. The Leray comparison and the long exact
sequences of the pairs therefore give
\[

             \cong H^k(Y/S^1,\partial(Y/S^1);R)=0
                            \qquad(k>5).                     \tag{D.T37}\hypertarget{tag-025I}{}\label{maps:eq:D.T37}
\]
The dimension bound can be read from an orbifold triangulation,
or from a finite good orbifold atlas and its relative cellular
cohomology. No division by three occurs in this comparison.

\[

                         \text{ is injective}.               \tag{D.T38}\hypertarget{tag-025J}{}\label{maps:eq:D.T38}
\]

with coefficients $R$. Restricting to the ordinary fibre $X$ gives
\[
                        \langle\mathcal P_3(u),[X]\rangle=0
                                     \quad\text{in }\mathbb Z/9.
                                                               \tag{D.T39}\hypertarget{tag-025K}{}\label{maps:eq:D.T39}
\]

refined Pontryagin class is zero as well. This also agrees with
ordinary localization, which yields $p_1=0$ because $w^2=1$;
that latter congruence alone would not have proved \eqref{maps:eq:D.T39}.

\item \emph{5. The stated concrete smooth model.}
The graph embedding in \eqref{maps:eq:D.T32} represents three times the generator.
Its oriented real rank-four normal bundle is trivial: the ambient
manifold is spin and $w_2(TS^2)=0$, and $w_2$ classifies such bundles

$\pi_2SO(4)=0$. The framed surgery preserves simple connectivity
and spin. Its integral sequence and duality give
$H_2=H_3=\mathbb Z/3$, with $b_3=0$.
The mod-three class from the first $S^2$ extends across the surgery
trace, since it evaluates to zero on the attaching sphere.
The original pair $(S^2\times S^4,u)$ spin-bounds
$S^2\times D^5$ over $K(\mathbb Z/3,2)$.
Thus the resulting model has zero spin-bordism class over this
Eilenberg--Mac Lane space. Zhubr's Theorem~3
\cite[p.795]{manZhubr75} identifies it, orientation-preservingly,
with every manifold in \eqref{maps:eq:D.T31}, since both classifying maps induce
isomorphisms on $H_2$ and both have $b_3=0$.

                         X^{C_3}=C_0\sqcup E.

\paragraph{One equivariant line on the partial completion.}

\[

\]
The cocycle quotient is $e^{2\pi i\omega(\lambda,\mu)}=1$ and the

\[
                \pi_1(Y)=\mathbb Z_\gamma\times F_t,
                  \qquad t=0\text{ or }1.
\]
The inverse group map kills the first three periods, retains $\gamma$
and the additive meridian, and replaces the ordinary meridian by the
inverse product. This proves torsion freeness.
The graph and cap maps above send every section sweep to zero in

and for an original cap both sweeps bound. Since $H_1(Y)$ is free,

\[

\]
Here $1/2=2$ in $\mathbb F_3$.
The connected circle acts trivially on ordinary cohomology. The only
possible outgoing differentials on $\alpha$ in the Borel sequence have
targets $H^2(BS^1;H^1(X;\mathbb F_3))$ and $H^3(BS^1;\mathbb F_3)$,

its isotopy to any group element is based and
$\pi_1(Y_{C_3})=\pi_1(Y)\times C_3$. Every finite isotropy section

$\rho_3(\lambda_j)\eta$, where the integral $\lambda_j$ form a basis

$U|_{Y_{C_3}}-\tfrac12\rho_3c_1^{C_3}(\mathcal D)$

The chart weights give $z(z-kT)=0$ and $\int_{C_0}z=1$. The restriction is
\[
             U|_{(C_0)_{S^1}}=\rho_3(Az),\qquad z(z-kT)=0.
             \tag{D.T34}\hypertarget{tag-025F}{}\label{maps:eq:D.T34}

$u=A^{-1}\alpha$ in $\mathbb F_3$; its inverse change is $\alpha=Au$.

\[
 H_5(K(\mathbb Z/3,2);\mathbb Z)=0,\qquad
 H_6(K(\mathbb Z/3,2);\mathbb Z)=
       \mathbb Z/9\langle\gamma_3(e)\rangle,

sends $[\mathbb {CP}^3]$ to $\gamma_3(e)$
\cite[Expos\'e~11, Theorems~1 and~4, pp.~11-09--11-14]{manCartan1955EML}.

$\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb Z/9,\mathbb Z/9)$. The detector is therefore
fixed by positive $\mathbb {CP}^3$ evaluation one:
\[
 Q_3:H^2(-;\mathbb F_3)\longrightarrow H^6(-;\mathbb Z/9),\qquad
 Q_3(\rho_3x)=\rho_9(x^3).

Its coefficient map is $\gamma_3(e)\mapsto1$, with inverse

\[

part of the diagonal carrier may be the iterated Alexander--Whitney
diagonal with augmentation one, and the carried homotopy identifies
any other such choice with it. Its product is consequently the
ordinary cube with coefficient one. This identifies Thomas's operation
with $Q_3$, including its coefficient map.

\[

identity and the vanishing on the dimension-one factor.

integer lift, and its inverse is multiplication by $w^3$ when

                  \quad\text{in }H^6(E_{S^1};\mathbb Z/9).
 \tag{D.T36}\hypertarget{tag-025H}{}\label{maps:eq:D.T36}
\]
Its C9 restriction also vanishes. Formula \eqref{maps:eq:D.T38} and

\[

                                   \quad\text{in }\mathbb Z/9.
 \tag{D.T39}\hypertarget{tag-025K}{}\label{maps:eq:D.T39}
\]

\paragraph{The oriented surgery model.}
Let $f:S^2\to S^2$ have degree three and let
$\iota:S^2\hookrightarrow S^4$ be an equatorial embedding. The map
$x\mapsto(f(x),\iota(x))$ is an embedding representing three times
the positive first-factor generator. Its oriented rank-four normal
bundle has $w_2=0$, since $S^2\times S^4$ is spin and
$w_2(TS^2)=0$. Oriented rank-four bundles on $S^2$ are classified by
this class, so the normal bundle is trivial. Its framing is unique
up to homotopy because $\pi_2SO(4)=0$.

map on $H_2$ is multiplication by three, giving
$H_2(W)=\mathbb Z/3$, $H_3(W)=0$, and $H_4(W)=\mathbb Z$.

$H_4(W)\to H_4(W,M_{3,0})$ equal to multiplication by three.

$H_2(M_{3,0})=H_3(M_{3,0})=\mathbb Z/3$ and $b_3=0$.

simple connectivity. The spin structure extends across the framed handle.

the attaching sphere evaluates to zero; the relative extension is
unique because $\pi_3K(\mathbb Z/3,2)=0$.

with the construction and uniqueness in \S4.1, now applies to $X$
and $M_{3,0}$
\cite[Theorem~3, p.~795; Theorem~5, p.~796; \S4.1, pp.~809--810]{manZhubr75}.

have $b_3=0$, and their spin-bordism classes coincide. The resulting
oriented diffeomorphism carries the positive surgery generator to $s$.
This proves \eqref{maps:eq:D.T32} and \eqref{maps:eq:D.T33}.
\end{proof}

\]

is its based peripheral insertion in \(K\).

\[
 ((\Lambda^2 A_i(d)-I)\eta,0)

 \tag{D.OW2}\hypertarget{tag-022X}{}\label{maps:eq:D.OW2}

\(A_i(d)=I\). Put \(N_m=\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}A_i(d)^j\).

\begin{enumerate}[label={$\langle1\rangle$\arabic*.},leftmargin=*]
\item \emph{The integral involution splitting.}
Put $g=\gcd(a,d)$. The prime-local proof in \ref{maps:src:D.2.37}
shows, without assuming $g=1$, that every torsion
prime of
\[
 C=(\Lambda^2\Lambda)_{\{A_i(d)\}}
\]
divides $g$. Its free rank is one. Under \eqref{maps:eq:D.OW1}
we may write $C\simeq\mathbb Z\oplus C_{\rm tor}$,
with $C_{\rm tor}$ of odd order. The regular graph
sequence is an exact sequence of abelian groups
\[
                 0\longrightarrow C\longrightarrow
           H_2(V)\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow0.      \tag{D.OW5}\hypertarget{tag-0230}{}\label{maps:eq:D.OW5}
\]
Fibre inversion is an actual involution of this
linear torus bundle. It acts by $+1$ on $C$ and
by $-1$ on $K$.

\item Let $A:H_2(V)\to\mathbb Z$ be evaluation by the
pullback of the marked weight-one class used in
\ref{maps:src:D.2.37}. It is invariant under inversion: this is
true on the old fibre and on all its generating
fixed sweeps, and therefore remains true on the
cover. Its restriction to $C$ is
\[
 g\,\omega',\qquad
 \omega'=(a/g)e_1^*e_2^*-(db/g)\delta^*\gamma^*,
\]
where $\omega'$ is the primitive free functional.
For any $x\in H_2(V)$, $x+\iota x$ belongs to $C$.
Hence
$2A(x)=A(x+\iota x)$ is divisible by $g$.
Since $g$ is odd, $A/g$ is an integral homomorphism.
Call it $B$.

\item We spell out the resulting splitting to avoid a
formality or invariant-descent assumption. Given
$k\in K$, choose a lift $x$ with $B(x)=0$, subtracting
a fibre generator if necessary. Then
$x+\iota x\in C_{\rm tor}$. Multiplication by two
is an automorphism of this finite group, so
\[
                  y=x-\tfrac12(x+\iota x)                 \tag{D.OW6}\hypertarget{tag-0231}{}\label{maps:eq:D.OW6}
\]
is a well-defined integral class with
$\iota y=-y$ and image $k$. If the lift $x$ is
changed by $c\in C_{\rm tor}$, the half term
changes by $c$, so $y$ is unchanged.
This constructs an additive section of \eqref{maps:eq:D.OW5}.
It is the unique section with $B=0$ and
anti-invariant image. Thus
$H_2(V)=C\oplus K$ with an actual integral marking,
including the odd torsion of $C$.

\item Every literal fixed-loop peripheral torus is
anti-invariant, since inversion reverses its
fibre circle and fixes the base circle. It
therefore has exactly its graph coordinate and
zero fibre coordinate in this splitting.
This remains true for the norm sweep of any
covering-torus loop: take the pushforward of
$\lambda\times S^1$ from the $m$-fold mapping-torus
cover, where $A^m=I$. It is anti-invariant and
has graph coordinate $N_m\lambda$.
This is the step that controls integral torsion
which a vertical alternating form alone cannot see.

\item \emph{The full finite and regular normal columns.}
On the $m$-fold boundary cover the normal meridian
is $m\theta-v$. The shear
$(x,t)\mapsto(x-tv,t)$ sends the product torus
of $\lambda$ and the covering base circle to
that norm sweep minus the regular torus
$\lambda\wedge v$. Pushing it to the ordinary
mapping torus and then to $V$, the preceding
anti-invariant description gives exactly the
first four columns of \eqref{maps:eq:D.OW3}.
There is no unknown torsion component in the
norm sweep.

\item For the affine meridian, use its commuting lifts
$\theta$ and $\mu=\theta^m v^{-1}$ in the boundary
group. Their torus is the fixed torus of $v$
and $\theta$, with the normal orientation
convention of \ref{maps:src:D.2.29}. Hence its image is
$(0,J_iv)$, the last column in \eqref{maps:eq:D.OW3}.
These loops generate the complete normal Thom
image, including torsion loops in the central
finite quotient. The proof of the general
freeness test \eqref{maps:eq:D.WP5} is unchanged.

\item \emph{Every nonfinite fibre kernel and its marked normal.}
All the unchanged caps in this construction have
torsion-free $H_2$. For the rank-two cusp this is
the explicit normalization calculation. For a
rank-one gamma cover the normalized components
are $S^2$ bundles of degree zero over a covered
two-torus, and consecutive double curves are
identified by translations; straightening those
translations gives the same free homology as a
cycle of spheres times $T^2$. Original
zero-degree additive caps have the permutation
mapping-torus homology of a Kodaira tree times
$S^1$, which is free. The nonzero-Chern originals
have the primitive Gysin presentations of
\ref{maps:src:D.2.32}--\ref{maps:src:D.2.33}, also free.

\item The covering square on regular fibres multiplies
bivectors by $\Lambda^2S_d$. The needed ranks come
from the actual caps, as follows. At the rank-two
zero the short-period map has Smith factors $(1,d)$.
In that basis its exterior-square difference has
primitive image of rank two, so the boundary has
$H_2=\mathbb Z^6$. The normalization calculation of
\ref{maps:src:D.2.34} gives $H^3(N)=\mathbb Z^2$. The two angular
normal tori are a primitive sublattice of boundary
homology and bound by their section-disc sweeps.
The pair sequence bounds its whole kernel by rank
two; hence they are exactly that kernel. In
particular the regular-fibre coinvariant of rank
four injects into the cap. This proves that the
rational fibre kernel is precisely the monodromy
image, without a local invariant-cycle assumption.

\item For the rank-one cap, the explicit cycle of
$\rho$ spheres times $T^2$ has four independent
nearby-fibre classes: the sum of the component
spheres, the surviving nodal-circle class times
each transverse circle, and the transverse
$T^2$ area. This is the full four-dimensional
fibre coinvariant, so again its kernel is exactly
the monodromy image over $\mathbb Q$. For an
original zero-degree additive cap, the permutation
mapping torus of the Kodaira tree gives the two
independent images: the nonzero multiplicity-weighted
whole-fibre class in the component-orbit space,
and the transverse $\delta\gamma$ area. These
are the full two-dimensional fibre coinvariant,
also for the original odd-star fibres. The
zero-degree multiplicative original has the same
four explicit classes as the nodal-cycle model.

\item Thus in every zero-degree case the rational
fibre kernel is exactly the inverse image of
the old one. For a nonzero-Chern original the
actual area and principal-bundle formulas give
the same statement directly. Since the target
$H_2$ is torsion free, the integral kernel is the
saturation of that rational kernel. This is
precisely \eqref{maps:eq:D.OW4}.

\item The full fixed-normal projections lift the old
bounding section-disc sweeps, as in \ref{maps:src:D.2.37}.
There is one previously isolated correction:
at a nonzero-Chern original multiplicative cap,
the vanishing-loop normal can differ from a
kernel cycle by an integral multiple of
$u_2\wedge\delta$. In \ref{maps:src:D.2.33} only its zero
alternating-form value was needed. Here it
vanishes in the full global fibre coinvariant.
Indeed, for all $172$ rows the elliptic matrices
$B_i$ satisfy the exact unit Smith certificate
\[
       \mathbb Z^2/\sum_i(B_i-I)\mathbb Z^2=0.             \tag{D.OW7}\hypertarget{tag-0232}{}\label{maps:eq:D.OW7}
\]
These $172$ matrices and their unit factors
are retained in
\path{records/manifolds_elliptic_coinvariants.json}.
Since every $A_i(d)$ fixes $\delta$,
\[
 (\Lambda^2A_i(d)-I)(\delta\wedge z)
                 =\delta\wedge(B_i-I)z
       \quad(z\in\mathbb Z^2).
\]
Consequently $\delta\wedge e_1$ and
$\delta\wedge e_2$ are zero integrally in $C$,
for every weight. This kills the correction
without any assumption on its integer value.

\item Subtracting these complete marked normals
from a boundary-kernel element leaves a
regular-fibre element. Its full image is
exactly \eqref{maps:eq:D.OW4}. Thus \eqref{maps:eq:D.OW2}--\eqref{maps:eq:D.OW4}
give the entire integral global kernel;
in particular a primitive fibre relation
that was only a torsion class in the boundary
has not been omitted.

\item \emph{Global homology and the remaining scope.}
The relative pair argument \eqref{maps:eq:D.WP11} does not
require the regular coinvariant to be free.
Finite and regular caps still have free
relative degree-two groups, and their
nonzero base-meridian coefficients make the
first relative map injective. Their full
degree-three images are now \eqref{maps:eq:D.OW3}.
The remaining caps still have free
$H^4$, so the final kernel in \eqref{maps:eq:D.WP11} is
free and the abelian-group extension splits.
The top component counts and rational ranks
are unchanged. Therefore \eqref{maps:eq:D.WP8} and the
entire duality table hold, with exactly the
full torsion cokernel computed here.

\item The vertical normal closures are also unchanged,
so the same all-order Seifert presentation
computes the full fundamental group.
The argument has not used a bound on weights
or logarithmic parameters. It uses oddness
only in dividing $g$ in the invariant functional
and in the unique half of \eqref{maps:eq:D.OW6}. When both
$a$ and $d$ are even, a two-primary ambiguity
can remain in that marking; this theorem
does not discard it.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

The first three entries of the \(\gamma\) column are multiplied by

With the last site omitted, put

The ordered product of the returns is the identity. The identities
\[
 (MN-I)x=(M-I)Nx+(N-I)x,\qquad
