\begin{corollary}[Open four-cells in the sphere targets]
\hypertarget{tag-036V}{}\label{wb:cusp-cone-literal-R4-open-cells}
Use the quotients, metrics and height sections of
\cref{wb:cusp-cone-angle-forgotten-sphere-carriers}.
For every admissible $T$, with $0<r_T<\epsilon$, put
\[
 U_{12,T}=\mathbb S_{12,T}^4\setminus\{*\},\qquad
 U_{24,T}=\mathbb S_{24,T}^4\setminus\{*\}.
\]
The restrictions of the specified quotient maps are homeomorphisms
\begin{equation}
 \rho_{12,T}\circ(c_T\times c_T):
 (Q_T\setminus K_T^{(1)})^2\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }U_{12,T},
 \hypertarget{tag-036G}{}\label{wb:cusp-cone-U12-homeomorphism}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 \rho_{24,T}:(C_T\setminus\{0\})^4
          \xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }U_{24,T}.
 \hypertarget{tag-036H}{}\label{wb:cusp-cone-U24-homeomorphism}
\end{equation}
Each $U_{\nu,T}$ is homeomorphic to $\mathbb R^4$ and is
topologically embedded in its ambient sphere, $S^6$ for $\nu=12$
and $S^8$ for $\nu=24$.  It is open in its moving four-sphere and
nonclosed both there and in its ambient sphere.  Its ambient closure
is precisely $\mathbb S_{\nu,T}^4$, and it is not open in that
ambient sphere.

For each fixed admissible $T$, the restriction to $U_{\nu,T}$ of the
assigned compact quotient metric is not globally isometric to
Euclidean $\mathbb R^4$.  The same assertion holds for the restriction
of any compatible metric on its compact ambient sphere.
For the assigned quotient metrics, every fixed radius-$R$ Euclidean
four-ball occurs isometrically as the entire midpoint ball in
$U_{12,T}$ whenever $T-C>4R$, and in $U_{24,T}$ whenever
$\ell_T>4R$, with the tail constant $C$ of
\cref{wb:cusp-cone-angle-forgotten-sphere-carriers}.
The isometries are the restrictions of the two displayed quotient maps,
after the marked Euclidean covering charts at the specified midpoints.
Both thresholds hold eventually as $T\to+\infty$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The basepoint fibres of the two quotient maps are
\[
 W_{12,T}=(K_T^{(1)}\times Q_T)\cup(Q_T\times K_T^{(1)}),\qquad
 W_{24,T}=\{(u_1,u_2,u_3,u_4):u_j=0\text{ for some }j\}.
\]
They identify no distinct points off those fibres.  If a closed subset
$A$ of $E$ is collapsed to one point, the restriction
$E\setminus A\to(E/A)\setminus\{*\}$ is a homeomorphism:
it is a continuous bijection, and every open subset of $E\setminus A$
is an open saturated subset of $E$.  Apply this observation to the
quotient identifications of
\cref{wb:cusp-cone-angle-forgotten-sphere-carriers}.
This proves both displayed homeomorphisms with their prescribed maps.

Here are coordinates and inverses.  The maps
\[
 u_T:(0,1)^2\longrightarrow Q_T\setminus K_T^{(1)},\quad
        a\longmapsto[Y_Ta],\qquad
 v_T:(0,1)\longrightarrow C_T\setminus\{0\},\quad
        a\longmapsto[\ell_Ta]
\]
are homeomorphisms.  The inverse of $u_T$ takes the two representatives
of $Y_T^{-1}y$ in $(0,1)$; changing the lift $y$ changes these
coordinates by integers.  The inverse of $v_T$ chooses the representative
in $(0,\ell_T)$ and divides by $\ell_T$.
Set
\[
 \eta(t)=\frac12\left(1+\frac{t}{\sqrt{1+t^2}}\right),\qquad
 \eta^{-1}(a)=\frac{2a-1}{2\sqrt{a(1-a)}}.
\]
The derivative of $\eta$ is positive, its limits are $0$ and $1$,
and $4\eta(t)(1-\eta(t))=(1+t^2)^{-1}$ proves the displayed inverse.
The homeomorphisms from $\mathbb R^4$ to the two open cells are
\[
 t\longmapsto\rho_{12,T}
   \bigl(c_Tu_T(\eta(t_1),\eta(t_2)),
         c_Tu_T(\eta(t_3),\eta(t_4))\bigr)
\]
and
\[
 t\longmapsto\rho_{24,T}
   \bigl([\ell_T\eta(t_1)],\ldots,[\ell_T\eta(t_4)]\bigr).
\]
Their inverses recover the uncollapsed coordinates by the two quotient
homeomorphisms, use $u_T^{-1}$ or $v_T^{-1}$, and then apply
$\eta^{-1}$ to each coordinate.

The compact height-section embeddings of
\cref{wb:cusp-cone-angle-forgotten-sphere-carriers} restrict to the
claimed embeddings.  Their images in the interiors of the ambient
cube quotients $[0,1]^6/\partial[0,1]^6$ and
$[0,1]^8/\partial[0,1]^8$ have coordinates
\[
 (r_T/\epsilon,a_1,a_2,r_T/\epsilon,a_3,a_4)
\]
and
\[
 (r_T/\epsilon,a_1,r_T/\epsilon,a_2,
                 r_T/\epsilon,a_3,r_T/\epsilon,a_4),
 \qquad a_j\in(0,1).
\]
The inverse on either image projects to the four $a_j$ coordinates.

moving sphere converging to each point of the open cell.  Thus neither
open cell is open in its ambient sphere.

Each open cell is the complement of a closed point in its moving

\[
 \operatorname{diam}(Q_T^2)\leq\|Y_T\|_{\mathrm{op}},\qquad
 \operatorname{diam}(C_T^4)\leq\ell_T.
\]

metrics therefore have these finite diameter bounds.  Any metric
compatible with the topology of the compact ambient sphere also has
finite diameter.  A surjective isometry from $\mathbb R^4$ would
preserve the unbounded distances between $0$ and $(n,0,0,0)$, which
contradicts each finite bound.

\[
 \widetilde y_T=Y_T(1/2,1/2)^{\mathsf T},\qquad
 b_{12,T}=(\widetilde y_T,\widetilde y_T),\qquad
 b_{24,T}=(\ell_T/2,\ell_T/2,\ell_T/2,\ell_T/2).
\]

$Q_T^2$ and $u\mapsto[b_{24,T}+u]$ in $C_T^4$.

of \eqref{wb:cusp-cone-S12-onto-exact-ball} and
\eqref{wb:cusp-cone-S24-onto-exact-ball}.
The inverses first recover the unique uncollapsed product point and
then its unique lift within Euclidean distance $R$ of $b_{\nu,T}$.
The midpoint distances from the collapsed loci are at least
$(T-C)/2$ and equal to $\ell_T/2$, respectively, so these entire
balls lie in the open cells at the stated thresholds.  The same
isometries apply to closed or open radius-$R$ balls.  The period
growth $\ell_T\to\infty$ and the fixed residual bound $C$ prove
the final eventuality assertion.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Null-homotopies of the moving four-spheres]
\hypertarget{tag-036Z}{}\label{wb:cusp-cone-moving-S4-null-homotopy}
For every native parameter with \(0<r_T=e^{-2\pi T}<\epsilon\),
the height sections
\[
 a_T:S_T^2\longrightarrow S^3,\qquad
 b_T:C_T\longrightarrow S^2
\]
of \cref{wb:cusp-cone-angle-forgotten-sphere-carriers} are based
null-homotopic. Their smash powers defining the moving four-spheres,
\[
 I_{12,T}=a_T^{\wedge2}:S_T^2\wedge S_T^2\longrightarrow S^6,
 \qquad
 I_{24,T}=b_T^{\wedge4}:C_T^{\wedge4}\longrightarrow S^8,
\]
are based null-homotopic. The induced integral homology maps are
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 (I_{12,T})_* &:H_4(S_T^2\wedge S_T^2;\mathbb Z)
                    \longrightarrow H_4(S^6;\mathbb Z)=0,\\
 (I_{24,T})_* &:H_4(C_T^{\wedge4};\mathbb Z)
                    \longrightarrow H_4(S^8;\mathbb Z)=0.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Thus the fundamental classes of both moving four-spheres have zero
image in their ambient targets.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Use the fixed reduced-suspension models
\[
 S^3=\Sigma_{\mathrm{red},\epsilon}Z_2,\qquad
 S^2=\Sigma_{\mathrm{red},\epsilon}(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z),
 \qquad Z_2=S_T^2,
\]
with both end sections and the based meridian collapsed to one point.
The exact sections, in the markings of the cited theorem, are
\[
 a_T(z)=[r_T,z],\qquad
 b_T([u])=[r_T,[u/\ell_T]],\qquad C_T=\mathbb R/\ell_T\mathbb Z.
\]
For \(0\leq s\leq1\), define
\[
 A_T(z,s)=[(1-s)r_T,z],\qquad
 B_T([u],s)=[(1-s)r_T,[u/\ell_T]].
\]
These are continuous compositions with the suspension quotients.
Replacing \(u\) by \(u+n\ell_T\), \(n\in\mathbb Z\), adds
an integer to its circle coordinate, so the second formula is
well defined. At \(s=0\) they are the specified sections, at
\(s=1\) they are constant on the collapsed zero-height section,
and at every time they take their source basepoints to the
collapsed based meridian.

The two smash homotopies are
\[
 ([z_1,z_2],s)\longmapsto[A_T(z_1,s),A_T(z_2,s)],
\]
\[
 ([u_1,u_2,u_3,u_4],s)\longmapsto
 [B_T([u_1],s),B_T([u_2],s),B_T([u_3],s),B_T([u_4],s)].
\]
Every source fat wedge maps to the target basepoint throughout.
The product-to-smash quotient, multiplied by the time interval, is
a continuous surjection from a compact space to a Hausdorff space,
and hence a quotient map. The displayed continuous product formulas
therefore descend to jointly continuous based homotopies on the
whole smash products. Their initial maps are \(I_{12,T}\) and
\(I_{24,T}\), and their terminal maps are constant.

The characteristic-square and characteristic-interval identifications
in the cited theorem orient both source smashes as four-spheres.
Homotopy invariance identifies their homology pushforwards with
those of constant maps, which factor through
\(H_4(\{*\};\mathbb Z)=0\). This proves the fundamental-class assertions.
\end{proof}

\hypertarget{tag-037K}{}\label{wb:cusp-cone-sphere-map-homotopy-status}
\StatementRecord{wb:cusp-cone-sphere-map-homotopy-status}{proved}{037K}{\SeriesRef{wb:cusp-cone-S24-sphere-map-null}, \SeriesRef{wb:cusp-cone-S12-sphere-map-null}, \SeriesRef{wb:cusp-null:thm}, \SeriesRef{mapsIII:angle-forgotten-one-copy-null}}

The maps \(S^{12}\to S^6\) and \(S^{24}\to S^8\) induce zero on all
positive-degree integral homology and cohomology groups and have zero
ordinary Hurewicz image.  They have no classical degree because source and
target dimensions differ.  The full four-copy map
\(\widehat q_\gamma^{\wedge4}:S^{24}\to S^8\) is based null-homotopic by
\cref{wb:cusp-cone-S24-sphere-map-null}.  The distinct two-copy map
\(\widehat q_3^{\wedge2}:S^{12}\to S^6\) is also based null-homotopic, by
\cref{wb:cusp-cone-S12-sphere-map-null}.  In both cases the vanishing is a
theorem about the full specified sphere-valued map, not merely its Hurewicz
image or the inclusion of a moving four-sphere. % checked carrier correction: one-copy-status
The one-copy class
\([\widehat q_3]\in\pi_6(S^3)\) is zero by the complete framed-torus
proof in \cref{wb:cusp-null:thm}.  Both this class and
\([\widehat q_\gamma]\in\pi_6(S^2)\) also vanish by the extension
homotopy in \cref{mapsIII:angle-forgotten-one-copy-null}.  That proof
uses the original formulas after forgetting the base angle and fixes

\begin{remark}[Homotopy and graded invariants of the sphere maps]
\hypertarget{tag-037K}{}\label{wb:cusp-cone-sphere-map-homotopy-status}
Use the based sphere identifications of
\cref{wb:cusp-cone-angle-forgotten-sphere-carriers}, and write
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 G_{12}&=\mu_{3,2}\widehat q_3^{\wedge2}\mu_{6,2}^{-1}:
                  S^{12}\longrightarrow S^6,\\
 G_{24}&=\mu_{2,4}\widehat q_\gamma^{\wedge4}\mu_{6,4}^{-1}:
                  S^{24}\longrightarrow S^8.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Here \(\mu_{n,r}:(S^n)^{\wedge r}\to S^{nr}\) is the
ordered characteristic-cube concatenation of that theorem, with
inverse given by splitting the nonboundary coordinates into blocks
and sending the boundary class to the smash basepoint.

The ordered quotient basis \((\widehat\gamma,\widehat u)\)
gives the mutually inverse torus maps
\[
 \beta:[a\widehat\gamma+b\widehat u]\longmapsto[a,b],\qquad
 \beta^{-1}:[a,b]\longmapsto[a\widehat\gamma+b\widehat u].
\]
They preserve the coordinate circle subgroups and hence induce
inverse skeleton-quotient maps and reduced-suspension maps.
In these coordinates the lattice projection is
\(p(a,b,c,d)=(a,b)\), and
\(\varepsilon_\gamma=\operatorname{pr}_1p\).
Consequently the long-period map \(\alpha\) of
\cref{mapsIII:angle-forgotten-one-copy-null} satisfies
\(\overline\pi_f=\beta\alpha\) and
\(\theta_\gamma=\operatorname{pr}_1\beta\alpha\).
On the punctured cusp the defining formulas are therefore
\[
 \widehat q_3(x)=[|t|,c(\beta\alpha(x))],\qquad
 \widehat q_\gamma(x)=[|t|,\operatorname{pr}_1\beta\alpha(x)].
\]
Both maps equal the suspension basepoint on \(W\) and outside
the cusp interior. These formulas identify them on all of \(X\)
with the two maps of the cited proposition, through the displayed
target homeomorphisms. That proposition supplies their based
null-homotopies, fixing the chosen \(x_0\in W\), and the based
null-homotopy of every positive smash power. Thus
\[
 [\widehat q_3]=0\in\pi_6(S^3),\qquad
 [\widehat q_\gamma]=0\in\pi_6(S^2),\qquad
 [G_{12}]=0\in\pi_{12}(S^6),\qquad
 [G_{24}]=0\in\pi_{24}(S^8).
\]

The positive-degree integral homology maps with a nonzero source
or target group are precisely
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 (G_{12})_* &: H_6(S^{12})=0\longrightarrow H_6(S^6)=\mathbb Z,\\
 (G_{12})_* &: H_{12}(S^{12})=\mathbb Z\longrightarrow H_{12}(S^6)=0,\\
 (G_{24})_* &: H_8(S^{24})=0\longrightarrow H_8(S^8)=\mathbb Z,\\
 (G_{24})_* &: H_{24}(S^{24})=\mathbb Z\longrightarrow H_{24}(S^8)=0.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Every displayed map is zero; all other positive-degree homology maps
have both groups zero. The integral cohomology pullbacks are zero
in every positive degree as well: the potentially nonzero source
groups \(H^6(S^6)\) and \(H^8(S^8)\) map into
\(H^6(S^{12})=0\) and \(H^8(S^{24})=0\), respectively.
In degree zero, all four induced maps are the identity on \(\mathbb Z\).
The ordinary Hurewicz maps are
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 h&:\pi_{12}(S^6)\longrightarrow H_{12}(S^6;\mathbb Z)=0,\\
 h&:\pi_{24}(S^8)\longrightarrow H_{24}(S^8;\mathbb Z)=0,
 \end{aligned}
\]
and send these two classes to \((G_{12})_*[S^{12}]=0\) and
\((G_{24})_*[S^{24}]=0\).

For maps \(g:M^n\to N^n\) between connected closed oriented
\(n\)-manifolds, ordinary degree is defined by
\(g_*[M]=\deg(g)[N]\) in \(H_n(N;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z[N]\).
Here the source fundamental classes map into
\(H_{12}(S^6)=0\) and \(H_{24}(S^8)=0\), while the target
fundamental classes generate \(H_6(S^6)\) and \(H_8(S^8)\).
These are the exact graded pushforwards; the ordinary degree
definition assigns no integer degree to either of the two maps.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[Exact Kummer extension through the cusp]
\hypertarget{tag-037X}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-extension-theorem}
\StatementRecord{wb:cusp-cover-extension-theorem}{proved}{037X}{\SeriesRef{wb:cusp-cover-source-action}, \SeriesRef{wb:cusp-cover-target-action}, \SeriesRef{wb:cusp-cover-source-factor}, \SeriesRef{wb:cusp-cover-maximal-chart-map}, \SeriesRef{wb:cusp-cover-basechange-local-ring}, \SeriesRef{wb:cusp-cover-triple-fibre-length}, \SeriesRef{wb:cusp-cover-double-fibre-length}, \SeriesRef{wb:cusp-cover-additive-fibre-map}, \SeriesRef{wb:cusp-cover-equivariance-computation}}

\mbox{}\ 
After shrinking the $v$-disc, the following statements hold.

\begin{enumerate}
\item The maps in \eqref{wb:cusp-cover-source-action} extend to a free,
properly discontinuous action on $Y^{(N)}$.  The quotient
\[
 f_N\colon N_0^{\langle N\rangle}
 :=Y^{(N)}/\bar\Lambda\longrightarrow\Delta_v
\]
is a proper holomorphic map from a smooth threefold.  Its central fibre
$W_N$ is reduced, irreducible, and nonnormal, and its normalization is a
toric del Pezzo surface of degree six.

\item Multiplication by $N$ on the cocharacter lattice defines a finite
flat toric morphism
\begin{equation}
 P_N\colon Y^{(N)}\longrightarrow Y,\qquad
 P_N(\xi_1,\xi_2,v)=(\xi_1^N,\xi_2^N,v^N),
 \hypertarget{tag-0389}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-toric-power-map}
\end{equation}
of degree $N^3$.  It is equivariant for
\eqref{wb:cusp-cover-source-action} and
\eqref{wb:cusp-cover-target-action}, hence descends to a finite flat map
\begin{equation}
 \kappa_N\colon N_0^{\langle N\rangle}\longrightarrow N_0,
 \qquad f_0\circ\kappa_N=\rho_N\circ f_N,
 \hypertarget{tag-037T}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-completed-map}
\end{equation}
of degree $N^3$.

\item The map $\kappa_N$ is etale over $v\ne0$, and
\begin{equation}
 \kappa_N^*W=NW_N,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Ram}(\kappa_N)=(N-1)W_N.
 \hypertarget{tag-037U}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-direct-ramification}
\end{equation}
For $N>1$, the branch support of the map to the original cusp family
is the whole central fibre. For $N=1$, the displayed formulas give the identity and the branch support is empty.

\item Let
\begin{equation}
 N_0[N]:=N_0\times_{\Delta_t}\Delta_v,
 \qquad t=v^N.
 \hypertarget{tag-037R}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-base-changed-target}
\end{equation}
Then $N_0[N]$ is normal and $\kappa_N$ factors uniquely as
\begin{equation}
 N_0^{\langle N\rangle}
 \xrightarrow{\ Q_N\ }N_0[N]
 \longrightarrow N_0.
 \hypertarget{tag-0384}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-relative-factorization}
\end{equation}
The map $Q_N$ has generic degree $N^2$.  For $N>1$ it is quasi-etale but
not flat: it is etale over the smooth locus of $N_0[N]$, and its non-etale
and nonflat loci are exactly the inverse images of the double and triple
strata of the base-changed central fibre.  For $N>1$, its degree $N^2>1$ proves that $Q_N$ is not a
normalization map. For $N=1$ it is the identity of the normal target.

\item On the reduced central fibres, the induced map
$W_N\to W$ has generic degree $N^2$.  It lifts to a commutative diagram
\begin{equation}
\begin{CD}
 E_N\simeq\mathrm{dP}_6 @>{[N]}>> E\simeq\mathrm{dP}_6\\
 @V{\nu_N}VV @VV{\nu}V\\
 W_N @>>> W,
\end{CD}
 \hypertarget{tag-0383}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-normalization-diagram}
\end{equation}
where $[N]$ is toric multiplication by $N$, of degree $N^2$, ramified
with index $N$ along each of the six toric boundary curves.  The diagram
respects the paired conductor curves and the two triple-point classes.

\item Over $v\ne0$, $Q_N$ is exactly the cover defined by
\[
 \mathbb Z\langle\widehat\gamma,\widehat u,
 N\widehat w,N\widehat\delta\rangle
 \subset
 \mathbb Z\langle\widehat\gamma,\widehat u,
 \widehat w,\widehat\delta\rangle.
\]
Its deck group is $(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z)^2$.  The pulled-back cusp
monodromy is $M_0^N$, and in the displayed cover basis it is $M_0$:
\begin{equation}
 S_N^{-1}M_0^NS_N=M_0,\qquad
 S_N=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,N,N).
 \hypertarget{tag-0381}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-monodromy-conjugacy}
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}



\begin{proof}
\begin{enumerate}[label={$\langle1\rangle$\arabic*.},leftmargin=*]
\item We prove the assertions in the order in which the constructions occur.

\item \medskip\noindent
\emph{The source action.}
For $\bar\lambda\in\bar\Lambda$, the integral linear map
\[
 \varphi_{\bar\lambda}(y,y_3)
 =(y+y_3B_0\bar\lambda,y_3)
\]
translates the height-one slice by the integral vector
$B_0\bar\lambda$.  It preserves the $A_2$ triangulation and hence induces
a toric automorphism $\Phi_{\bar\lambda}$ of $Y^{(N)}$.  On the dense
torus this automorphism is
\[
 \Phi_{\bar\lambda}(\xi,v)
 =(v^{B_0\bar\lambda}\xi,v).
\]
Multiplication by the nowhere-zero holomorphic function
$c^{(N)}_{\bar\lambda}(v)$ extends across every toric chart.  Since
$C_N(v)\bar\lambda$ is additive in $\bar\lambda$, the resulting maps
satisfy
$\Psi^{(N)}_{\bar\lambda}\Psi^{(N)}_{\bar\mu}
=\Psi^{(N)}_{\bar\lambda+\bar\mu}$.

\item For completeness, freeness and proper discontinuity can be checked
directly.  Put
\[
 R_N(v):=-2\pi\operatorname{Im}C_N(v).
\]
It is bounded at $v=0$.  At a dense-torus point fixed by
$\bar\lambda$, logarithmic absolute values give
\[
 \log|v|B_0\bar\lambda+R_N(v)\bar\lambda=0.
\]
Choose the disc so small that
$|\log|v||>2\|R_N\|_\infty$.  Because $B_0$ is orthogonal, the last
equality is impossible for $\bar\lambda\ne0$.  On the central fibre,
$\Psi^{(N)}_{\bar\lambda}$ translates every bounded cell by the nonzero
vector $B_0\bar\lambda$, so it fixes no toric orbit.

\item For a dense-torus point set
\[
 y(\xi,v)=\frac{(\log|\xi_1|,\log|\xi_2|)}{\log|v|},
 \qquad
 B_{N,v}=B_0+\frac{R_N(v)}{\log|v|}.
\]
Then
\[
 y(\Psi^{(N)}_{\bar\lambda}(\xi,v))
 =y(\xi,v)+B_{N,v}\bar\lambda,
 \qquad
 |B_{N,v}\bar\lambda|\ge\tfrac12|\bar\lambda|.
\]
% checked carrier correction: compact-chart-control
The logarithmic positions of an entire affine toric chart need not be
bounded. The required assertion is about its compact subsets, and follows
as follows. In a maximal unimodular chart write its height-one rays as
$(b_0,1),(b_1,1),(b_2,1)$ and its coordinates as $w_0,w_1,w_2$.
On its dense torus,
\[
 v=w_0w_1w_2,\qquad
 y=\frac{\log|\xi|}{\log|v|}
   =\sum_{i=0}^2\lambda_i b_i,\qquad
 \lambda_i=\frac{\log|w_i|}{\log|v|},\qquad
 \sum_i\lambda_i=1.
\]
For a compact subset of this chart all $|w_i|$ have a common upper
bound $M\ge1$. When $|v|<1$, this gives
$\lambda_i\ge-\log M/|\log|v||$. Thus its logarithmic positions remain
in a bounded neighbourhood of the fixed triangle as $v\to0$.
On a closed annulus away from zero, the product identity and upper
bounds also bound each $|w_i|$ below. Hence the same boundedness holds
there. Every point of a compact set has a neighbourhood whose closure
is compact in one maximal chart.  Choose a finite such cover;
the intersections with these compact closures give finitely many
compact chart pieces covering the original set.  Applying the
preceding estimate to these pieces bounds all of its logarithmic
positions on the dense-torus locus.

\item For the modified action,
$y\mapsto y+B_{N,v}\bar\lambda$ and
$|B_{N,v}\bar\lambda|\ge|\bar\lambda|/2$.
Consequently only finitely many translates of one compact set can
meet another on the dense torus. At $v=0$, choose finitely many
maximal charts covering the two compact sets. A translate meeting
both must send a face of one of their triangles to a face of another.
There are finitely many pairs of faces and at most one translation
for each pair; thus the same finiteness holds at the central fibre.
This proves proper discontinuity without asserting boundedness of
whole affine charts.

\item To prove that $f_N$ is proper, reduce
$B_{N,v}^{-1}y$ modulo $\mathbb Z^2$ for $v\ne0$. The resulting $y$
lies in one bounded set, uniformly on the chosen small disc. Choose
an $A_2$ triangle containing $y$. Its barycentric coordinates are
nonnegative, and the corresponding toric coordinates satisfy
$|w_i|\le1$. Only finitely many triangles meet that bounded set.
Fix a closed subdisc strictly inside the chosen action disc.
Every orbit over that subdisc has a representative in finitely
many closed unit polydiscs intersected with its inverse image.
These intersections are closed subsets of compact polydiscs
in the ambient smooth Hausdorff toric space, and all lie in the
domain where the modified action is defined. At $v=0$, vertex translations move a component containing the
point to a fixed component; that component is the compact toric
surface with hexagonal star. Adding this compact component gives
a compact set mapping onto the quotient above a closed subdisc.
The inverse image of any compact subset of the base is a closed
subset of this compact image, and is therefore compact.

\item The central-fibre and
normalization assertions follow exactly from the height-one fan: locally
$v$ is the product of the coordinates belonging to the rays through a
cell, every component occurs with multiplicity one, the lattice action is
transitive on vertices, and the star of a vertex is the complete smooth
hexagonal fan.

\item \medskip\noindent
\emph{The toric map and equivariance.}
Multiplication by $N$ on $N'$ sends every cone $\sigma\in\Sigma$ onto
itself as a real cone.  It therefore defines the toric morphism $P_N$.
For a maximal cone, let $z_0,z_1,z_2$ be the target characters dual to its
three primitive height-one ray generators, and let $w_0,w_1,w_2$ be the
corresponding source characters.  The map on convergent local rings is
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb C\{z_0,z_1,z_2\}\longrightarrow
\mathbb C\{w_0,w_1,w_2\},\qquad z_i\longmapsto w_i^N.
 \hypertarget{tag-0380}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-maximal-chart-map}
\end{equation}
The target-chart preimage is the corresponding source chart, and the
right-hand ring is free of rank $N^3$ over the left-hand ring, with basis
\[
 \{w_0^{a_0}w_1^{a_1}w_2^{a_2}:0\le a_i<N\}.
\]
Thus $P_N$ is finite flat of degree $N^3$ on every maximal chart, hence
globally.

\item The choice \eqref{wb:cusp-cover-source-factor} satisfies equivariance by the following exact identity.
Indeed, writing powers coordinatewise,
\begin{align}
 P_N\Psi^{(N)}_{\bar\lambda}(\xi,v)
 &=\bigl((c^{(N)}_{\bar\lambda}(v))^N
          v^{NB_0\bar\lambda}\xi^N,v^N\bigr)\\
 &=\bigl(c_{\bar\lambda}(v^N)
          (v^N)^{B_0\bar\lambda}\xi^N,v^N\bigr)\\
 &=\Psi_{\bar\lambda}P_N(\xi,v).
 \hypertarget{tag-037W}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-equivariance-computation}
\end{align}
Consequently $P_N$ descends to \eqref{wb:cusp-cover-completed-map}.  To see
finiteness and flatness after the infinite-lattice quotient without any
implicit descent theorem, take an evenly covered open set in $N_0$ and
one of its lifts $V\subset Y$.  Equivariance gives a unique representative
of every source orbit above that open set whose image lies in $V$; two
such representatives cannot differ by a nontrivial lattice translate.
The descended map is therefore locally identified with
$P_N^{-1}(V)\to V$.  It is finite flat of degree $N^3$ by
\eqref{wb:cusp-cover-maximal-chart-map}.

\item In the same chart the base characters are
\[
 t=z_0z_1z_2,\qquad v=w_0w_1w_2,\qquad P_N^*t=v^N.
\]
The Jacobian determinant of \eqref{wb:cusp-cover-maximal-chart-map} is
\[
 N^3(w_0w_1w_2)^{N-1}=N^3v^{N-1}.
\]
This proves \eqref{wb:cusp-cover-direct-ramification}; the local quotient
maps are biholomorphisms, so the calculation is unchanged downstairs.

\item \medskip\noindent
\emph{The relative degree-$N^2$ factor.}
The equality
\((f_0\circ\kappa_N)([\xi,v])=v^N=(\rho_N\circ f_N)([\xi,v])\)
gives the factorization
\eqref{wb:cusp-cover-relative-factorization}.  At a triple point the exact
local-ring map is
\begin{equation}
 \begin{gathered}
 A_N:=
 \frac{\mathbb C\{z_0,z_1,z_2,v\}}
      {(z_0z_1z_2-v^N)},
 \qquad
 B:=\mathbb C\{w_0,w_1,w_2\},\\
 A_N\longrightarrow B,\qquad
 z_i\longmapsto w_i^N,\qquad
 v\longmapsto w_0w_1w_2.
 \end{gathered}
 \hypertarget{tag-037S}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-basechange-local-ring}
\end{equation}
Let
\[
 G_N=\{(\varepsilon_0,\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2)\in\mu_N^3:
       \varepsilon_0\varepsilon_1\varepsilon_2=1\}
 \simeq\mu_N^2
\]
act diagonally on $B$.  A monomial
$w_0^{a_0}w_1^{a_1}w_2^{a_2}$ is $G_N$-invariant if and only if
\[
 a_0\equiv a_1\equiv a_2\pmod N.
\]
Writing their common residue as $r$, with $0\le r<N$, expresses that
monomial uniquely in the form
\[
 (w_0w_1w_2)^r
 (w_0^N)^{b_0}(w_1^N)^{b_1}(w_2^N)^{b_2}.
\]
The same coefficientwise argument applies to convergent power series.
Hence
\begin{equation}
 A_N=B^{G_N}.
 \hypertarget{tag-037Z}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-invariant-ring}
\end{equation}
It follows that $A_N$ is normal, that the map has generic degree
$|G_N|=N^2$, and that it is a finite quotient rather than a normalization.
The corresponding face-chart calculations prove normality along the
double and smooth strata as well, so $N_0[N]$ is normal everywhere.

\item The stabilizer in $G_N$ is trivial when none or exactly one of the $w_i$
vanishes, is isomorphic to $\mu_N$ when exactly two vanish, and is all of
$G_N$ when all three vanish.  Thus $Q_N$ is etale in codimension one and
has no ramification divisor, but it is not etale above the double and
triple strata.  It is also nonflat at every such point when $N>1$.  At a
triple point the closed fibre of \eqref{wb:cusp-cover-basechange-local-ring}
has length
\begin{align}
 \dim_{\mathbb C}
 \frac{\mathbb C\{w_0,w_1,w_2\}}
      {(w_0^N,w_1^N,w_2^N,w_0w_1w_2)}
 &=N^3-(N-1)^3\\
 &=3N^2-3N+1,
 \hypertarget{tag-038A}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-triple-fibre-length}
\end{align}
which exceeds the generic rank $N^2$.  At a point of a double stratum,
localizing at the nonzero third coordinate and choosing its holomorphic
$N$th root reduces the ramified factor to
\[
 \frac{\mathbb C\{z_0,z_1,v\}}{(z_0z_1-v^N)}
\longrightarrow\mathbb C\{w_0,w_1\},\qquad
 z_i\longmapsto w_i^N,\quad v\longmapsto w_0w_1.
\]
Its local generic rank is $N$, whereas its closed fibre has length
\begin{equation}
 \dim_{\mathbb C}
 \frac{\mathbb C\{w_0,w_1\}}
      {(w_0^N,w_1^N,w_0w_1)}=2N-1>N.
 \hypertarget{tag-037V}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-double-fibre-length}
\end{equation}
The remaining transverse nonzero torus coordinate is etale locally.
Equations \eqref{wb:cusp-cover-triple-fibre-length} and
\eqref{wb:cusp-cover-double-fibre-length}, together with etaleness elsewhere,
identify the nonflat locus exactly.

\item \medskip\noindent
\emph{The regular fibres and monodromy.}
Choose a logarithm $r$ with $v=e^{2\pi ir}$.  The target period matrix at
$t=v^N$ is
\[
 Z(Nr)=NrB_0+C(v^N),
\]
whereas the source residual action is determined by
\[
 Z_N(r)=rB_0+\frac1NC(v^N)=\frac1N Z(Nr).
\]
The source fibre is therefore
\[
 \frac{\mathbb C^2}{\mathbb Z^2+Z_N(r)\mathbb Z^2},
\]
and multiplication by $N$ on $\mathbb C^2$ maps it to the target fibre.
Equivalently, in the unscaled additive coordinate it is the identity map
\begin{equation}
 \frac{\mathbb C^2}
      {N\mathbb Z^2+Z(Nr)\mathbb Z^2}
 \longrightarrow
 \frac{\mathbb C^2}
      {\mathbb Z^2+Z(Nr)\mathbb Z^2}.
 \hypertarget{tag-037P}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-additive-fibre-map}
\end{equation}
The imaginary part of $Z(Nr)$ is invertible on a regular fibre, so its
period lattice meets $\mathbb Z^2$ trivially in the required real sense;
the index in \eqref{wb:cusp-cover-additive-fibre-map} is $N^2$.  Its deck
group is $(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z)^2$.  In the ordered lattice basis
$(\widehat\gamma,\widehat u,\widehat w,\widehat\delta)$, this is exactly
the sublattice obtained by $S_N$.  Since $M_0=I+R$ with $R^2=0$ and
$R(a,b,c,d)=(0,0,b,-a)$, one has
\[
 M_0^N=I+NR,\qquad S_N^{-1}M_0^NS_N=M_0,
\]
proving \eqref{wb:cusp-cover-monodromy-conjugacy}.

\item \medskip\noindent
\emph{The central normalization and conductor.}
Multiplication by $N$ fixes every ray of $\Sigma$.  It therefore maps a
chosen source component of the toric central fibre to the corresponding
target component.  The star of that ray is the hexagonal fan, so the
restriction is the toric power map
$[N]\colon\mathrm{dP}_6\to\mathrm{dP}_6$.  On its dense two-torus it has
degree $N^2$; in each toric boundary chart it is an $N$th-power map in the
normal coordinate, hence has ramification index $N$ along all six boundary
curves.  Equation \eqref{wb:cusp-cover-equivariance-computation} says that
the source and target lattice identifications commute with this map.
Consequently opposite boundary curves, their conductor identifications,
and the two translation-orbits of triangle vertices descend compatibly.
This proves \eqref{wb:cusp-cover-normalization-diagram} and completes the
proof.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Kummer extension through the cusp]
\hypertarget{tag-037X}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-extension-theorem}
Fix $N\geq1$.  For a sufficiently small $r>0$, take the compatible
disc representatives
\[
 \Delta_v=\{|v|<r\},\qquad \Delta_t=\{|t|<r^N\},\qquad
 \Delta_v=\rho_N^{-1}(\Delta_t),
\]
and restrict the target cusp family to $\Delta_t$.  The holomorphic
germ $C$ is represented on a disc containing $\{|z|<r\}$.
With the actions \eqref{wb:cusp-cover-target-action} and
\eqref{wb:cusp-cover-source-action}, the following statements hold.

\begin{enumerate}
\item The source action extends freely and properly discontinuously to
$Y^{(N)}$.  Its quotient
\[
 f_N\colon N_0^{\langle N\rangle}:=Y^{(N)}/\bar\Lambda
 \longrightarrow\Delta_v
\]
is a proper holomorphic map from a smooth threefold.  Its central fibre
$W_N$ is reduced, irreducible and nonnormal, with normalization the
toric del Pezzo surface of degree six.

\item Multiplication by $N$ on the cocharacter lattice defines a finite
flat toric map of degree $N^3$,
\begin{equation}
 P_N\colon Y^{(N)}\longrightarrow Y,\qquad
 P_N(\xi_1,\xi_2,v)=(\xi_1^N,\xi_2^N,v^N).
 \hypertarget{tag-0389}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-toric-power-map}
\end{equation}
It is equivariant for the source and target lattice actions and descends
to a finite flat map of degree $N^3$,
\begin{equation}
 \kappa_N\colon N_0^{\langle N\rangle}\longrightarrow N_0,
 \qquad f_0\circ\kappa_N=\rho_N\circ f_N.
 \hypertarget{tag-037T}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-completed-map}
\end{equation}

\item The map $\kappa_N$ is \textup{\'etale} away from $W_N$, and
\begin{equation}
 \kappa_N^*W=NW_N,\qquad
 \operatorname{Ram}(\kappa_N)=(N-1)W_N.
 \hypertarget{tag-037U}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-direct-ramification}
\end{equation}
Its branch support is all of $W$ for $N>1$ and is empty for $N=1$.

\item The base-changed target
\begin{equation}
 N_0[N]:=N_0\times_{\Delta_t}\Delta_v,\qquad t=v^N,
 \hypertarget{tag-037R}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-base-changed-target}
\end{equation}
is normal.  There is a unique factorization
\begin{equation}
 N_0^{\langle N\rangle}
 \xrightarrow{\ Q_N\ }N_0[N]\longrightarrow N_0,
 \qquad Q_N(x)=(\kappa_N(x),f_N(x)).
 \hypertarget{tag-0384}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-relative-factorization}
\end{equation}
The finite map $Q_N$ has generic degree $N^2$.  For $N>1$ it is
quasi-\textup{\'etale}: its non-\textup{\'etale} and nonflat loci are
exactly the inverse images of the double and triple strata of the
base-changed central fibre, and it is \textup{\'etale} over the smooth
locus of $N_0[N]$.  The degree $N^2>1$ then excludes a normalization
morphism.  At $N=1$, both $\kappa_1$ and $Q_1$ are identities under
the coordinate identification of the source and target families and the
base-change isomorphism
$N_0\xrightarrow{\sim}N_0[1]$, $y\mapsto(y,f_0(y))$.

\item The map on reduced central fibres has generic degree $N^2$ and
lifts to the commutative diagram
\begin{equation}
 \begin{CD}
 E_N\simeq\mathrm{dP}_6 @>{[N]}>> E\simeq\mathrm{dP}_6\\
 @V{\nu_N}VV @VV{\nu}V\\
 W_N @>>> W.
 \end{CD}
 \hypertarget{tag-0383}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-normalization-diagram}
\end{equation}
Here $[N]$ is toric multiplication by $N$.  It has degree $N^2$ and
ramification index $N$ along each of the six toric boundary curves.
The square respects the paired conductor curves and both triple-point
classes.

\item Over $v\ne0$, the map $Q_N$ is the connected cover with fibre
lattice inclusion
\[
 \mathbb Z\langle\widehat\gamma,\widehat u,
 N\widehat w,N\widehat\delta\rangle
 \subset
 \mathbb Z\langle\widehat\gamma,\widehat u,
 \widehat w,\widehat\delta\rangle.
\]
Its deck group on the punctured family is $(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z)^2$.
The pulled-back target cusp monodromy is $M_0^N$, and its matrix in
the cover basis is $M_0$:
\begin{equation}
 S_N^{-1}M_0^NS_N=M_0,\qquad
 S_N=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,N,N).
 \hypertarget{tag-0381}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-monodromy-conjugacy}
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The maximal cones of the prescribed fan come from the integer translates
of $\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,e_2)$ and
$\operatorname{conv}(e_1,e_2,e_1+e_2)$ at height one.  Their three ray
generators form unimodular bases.  For the first triangle, source
coordinates are
\[
 (w_0,w_1,w_2)=\left(\frac{v}{\xi_1\xi_2},\xi_1,\xi_2\right),
 \qquad v=w_0w_1w_2.
\]
For the second they are
$(v/\xi_2,v/\xi_1,\xi_1\xi_2/v)$, again with product $v$.
Integer translations give the remaining smooth maximal charts.
Multiplication by $N$ preserves every cone and pulls each character
back to its $N$th power.  The preimage of a target maximal chart is
the corresponding source chart, and its local-ring map is
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb C\{z_0,z_1,z_2\}\longrightarrow
 \mathbb C\{w_0,w_1,w_2\},\qquad z_i\longmapsto w_i^N.
 \hypertarget{tag-0380}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-maximal-chart-map}
\end{equation}
The source ring is free over the target ring with basis
$w_0^{a_0}w_1^{a_1}w_2^{a_2}$, $0\leq a_i<N$.  Thus $P_N$ is finite
flat of degree $N^3$.  The compatible discs make the restricted source
the full preimage of the restricted target.

The monomial part of the source action comes from the integral fan
automorphism
\[
 (p,h)\longmapsto(p+hB_0\bar\lambda,h).
\]
It translates the height-one triangulation by $B_0\bar\lambda$.
Multiplication by $c^{(N)}_{\bar\lambda}(v)$ multiplies each chart
coordinate by a monomial in holomorphic units, so it also extends to
the charts.  Additivity in $\bar\lambda$ gives the group law.
Since $NC_N(v)=C(v^N)$, direct substitution yields
\begin{align}
 P_N\Psi^{(N)}_{\bar\lambda}(\xi,v)
 &=\bigl((c^{(N)}_{\bar\lambda}(v))^N
             v^{NB_0\bar\lambda}\xi^N,v^N\bigr)\\
 &=\bigl(c_{\bar\lambda}(v^N)
             (v^N)^{B_0\bar\lambda}\xi^N,v^N\bigr)
 =\Psi_{\bar\lambda}P_N(\xi,v).
 \hypertarget{tag-037W}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-equivariance-computation}
\end{align}
The identity extends from the dense torus to every chart.

The target lattice action is free and properly discontinuous by the
cusp construction used in Theorem~\ref{maps:src:B.4.1}.
A source point fixed by $\bar\lambda$ would map
to a target point fixed by the same element, so the source action is
free.  For a compact source set $K$, an intersection
$\Psi^{(N)}_{\bar\lambda}(K)\cap K\ne\varnothing$ implies
$\Psi_{\bar\lambda}(P_N(K))\cap P_N(K)\ne\varnothing$.
Only finitely many lattice elements have this property.  The source
quotient is therefore a smooth threefold.

Choose an open set $U\subset Y$ with disjoint nontrivial lattice
translates.  Equivariance makes the translates of $P_N^{-1}(U)$
disjoint as well, and the quotient identifies this preimage with
$\kappa_N^{-1}(U/\bar\Lambda)$.  In these local charts $\kappa_N$
is $P_N$, hence is finite flat of degree $N^3$.  The identity
$f_0\kappa_N=\rho_Nf_N$ follows from $P_N^*t=v^N$.
The map $f_0\kappa_N$ is proper.  For a compact $K\subset\Delta_v$,
the set $f_N^{-1}(K)$ is closed in the compact set
$(f_0\kappa_N)^{-1}(\rho_N(K))$, which proves that $f_N$ is proper.

The local equation $v=w_0w_1w_2$ makes $W_N$ reduced.  Before the
lattice quotient its components are the toric divisors $D_p$ indexed
by $p\in\mathbb Z^2$.  The action sends $D_p$ to
$D_{p+B_0\bar\lambda}$.  Because $B_0\bar\Lambda=\mathbb Z^2$,
the action is transitive on components and no nonzero element
stabilizes one.  Thus $W_N$ is irreducible.

The normalization is obtained by separating the local coordinate
branches.  More explicitly, for $1\leq k\leq3$ the natural injection
\[
 \frac{\mathbb C\{w_0,w_1,w_2\}}{(w_0\cdots w_{k-1})}
 \longrightarrow
 \prod_{i=0}^{k-1}
 \frac{\mathbb C\{w_0,w_1,w_2\}}{(w_i)}
\]
is finite, has the same total ring of fractions, and has normal target.
Its injectivity follows from
$\bigcap_{i<k}(w_i)=(w_0\cdots w_{k-1})$; it is the integral closure.
These maps glue, and the quotient of the disjoint components is
identified with $D_0$.  The identity of the two copies of the fan
identifies $D_0$ with the normalization $E$ of the target cusp.
Its star is the smooth hexagonal fan of $\mathrm{dP}_6$.
The two branches at an open double stratum prove nonnormality of $W_N$.

The Jacobian of \eqref{wb:cusp-cover-maximal-chart-map} is
\[
 N^3w_0^{N-1}w_1^{N-1}w_2^{N-1}=N^3v^{N-1}.
\]
Together with $P_N^*t=v^N$, this proves
\eqref{wb:cusp-cover-direct-ramification}.  The local period quotients
are biholomorphisms.  For $N>1$, every component of the central fibre
has ramification index $N$ and maps onto its target component, so the
branch support is $W$.  For $N=1$ the Jacobian is one.

The map $Q_N(x)=(\kappa_N(x),f_N(x))$ gives the unique factorization
through the fibre product.  At a triple point its local form is
\begin{equation}
 \begin{gathered}
 A_N:=\frac{\mathbb C\{z_0,z_1,z_2,v\}}
              {(z_0z_1z_2-v^N)},\qquad
 B:=\mathbb C\{w_0,w_1,w_2\},\\
 A_N\longrightarrow B,\qquad
 z_i\longmapsto w_i^N,\qquad v\longmapsto w_0w_1w_2.
 \end{gathered}
 \hypertarget{tag-037S}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-basechange-local-ring}
\end{equation}
Let
\[
 G_N=\{(\varepsilon_0,\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2)\in\mu_N^3:
          \varepsilon_0\varepsilon_1\varepsilon_2=1\}
 \simeq\mu_N^2
\]
act diagonally on $B$.  A monomial $w_0^{a_0}w_1^{a_1}w_2^{a_2}$
is invariant precisely when $a_0\equiv a_1\equiv a_2\pmod N$.
Writing the common residue as $r$, $0\leq r<N$, gives its unique form
\[
 (w_0w_1w_2)^r(w_0^N)^{b_0}(w_1^N)^{b_1}(w_2^N)^{b_2}.
\]
Grouping a convergent series into these finitely many residue classes
gives the same normal form.  The monomials are linearly independent,
and hence
\begin{equation}
 A_N=B^{G_N}.
 \hypertarget{tag-037Z}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-invariant-ring}
\end{equation}
This is a finite inclusion: the monomial generators for $B$ over the
original target ring also generate it over $A_N$.  An element of
$\operatorname{Frac}(B^{G_N})$ integral over $B^{G_N}$ is integral
over the normal ring $B$, lies in $B$, and is invariant.  Thus $A_N$
is normal.  The group is free on the dense torus and has order $N^2$,
so the relative degree is $N^2$.

On the source dense torus this group is the phase action
\[
 (\eta_1,\eta_2)\cdot(\xi_1,\xi_2,v)
       =(\eta_1\xi_1,\eta_2\xi_2,v),\qquad \eta_i\in\mu_N.
\]
In the first chart its identification with $G_N$ is
$(\eta_1,\eta_2)\mapsto((\eta_1\eta_2)^{-1},\eta_1,\eta_2)$.
This action extends torically and commutes with the period action.
The chart invariant rings therefore identify its global quotient
with $N_0[N]$.

At a double stratum the local target is
$\{z_0z_1=v^N\}$ times a smooth coordinate, and at a smooth point
of the central fibre it is $\{z_0=v^N\}$ times two smooth coordinates.
Away from the central fibre the base change is \textup{\'etale}.
These descriptions prove normality everywhere.  For $N>1$, the
singular locus is precisely the double and
triple strata, as follows by differentiating the local equations.
The stabilizer in $G_N$ is trivial when at most one of the $w_i$
vanishes, is $\mu_N$ when exactly two vanish, and is $G_N$ when all
three vanish.  The quotient is \textup{\'etale} where the stabilizer
is trivial.  A smooth source cannot be \textup{\'etale} over a singular
target, so the double and triple strata give exactly the non-\textup{\'etale}
locus.  This locus has codimension at least two in the source.

At a triple point the closed fibre length is
\begin{align}
 \dim_{\mathbb C}
 \frac{\mathbb C\{w_0,w_1,w_2\}}
      {(w_0^N,w_1^N,w_2^N,w_0w_1w_2)}
 &=N^3-(N-1)^3\\
 &=3N^2-3N+1.
 \hypertarget{tag-038A}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-triple-fibre-length}
\end{align}
Indeed a monomial basis has $0\leq a_i<N$ and at least one $a_i=0$.
For $N>1$, the excess over the generic rank $N^2$ is
$(N-1)(2N-1)>0$.
At a double stratum, choosing a root of the nonzero transverse
coordinate separates $N$ local branches.  Each has generic degree $N$
and a two-dimensional factor
\[
 \frac{\mathbb C\{z_0,z_1,v\}}{(z_0z_1-v^N)}
 \longrightarrow\mathbb C\{w_0,w_1\},\qquad
 z_i\longmapsto w_i^N,\quad v\longmapsto w_0w_1.
\]
Its closed fibre has basis $1,w_0,\ldots,w_0^{N-1},
w_1,\ldots,w_1^{N-1}$ and length
\begin{equation}
 \dim_{\mathbb C}
 \frac{\mathbb C\{w_0,w_1\}}
      {(w_0^N,w_1^N,w_0w_1)}=2N-1.
 \hypertarget{tag-037V}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-double-fibre-length}
\end{equation}
For $N>1$ this exceeds the local generic rank $N$.
Finite flat local modules have closed fibre dimension equal to their
generic rank.  For $N>1$ these excess lengths prove nonflatness at every
double and triple point; \textup{\'etaleness} elsewhere proves flatness there.
Since $N_0[N]$ is normal, its normalization is its identity.  The
degree $N^2>1$ for $N>1$ proves that $Q_N$ is not that normalization map.

For the regular fibres put $v=e^{2\pi i s_v}$, so
$t=e^{2\pi iNs_v}$.
The source and target matrices satisfy
\[
 Z_N(s_v)=s_vB_0+\frac1N C(v^N),\qquad
 Z(Ns_v)=NZ_N(s_v).
\]
The logarithmic map is $\zeta\mapsto N\zeta$.  For
$\Pi_{\mathrm{source}}=[Z_N(s_v)\mid I]$ and
$\Pi_{\mathrm{target}}=[Z(Ns_v)\mid I]$ its precise lattice identity is
\[
 N\Pi_{\mathrm{source}}=\Pi_{\mathrm{target}}S_N.
\]
The target period map is a real isomorphism, and the displayed equality
makes the source period group a full lattice as well.  After the
explicit coordinate change $\widetilde\zeta=N\zeta$, the fibre map is
\begin{equation}
 \frac{\mathbb C^2}{N\mathbb Z^2+Z(Ns_v)\mathbb Z^2}
 \longrightarrow
 \frac{\mathbb C^2}{\mathbb Z^2+Z(Ns_v)\mathbb Z^2},
 \qquad [\widetilde\zeta]\longmapsto[\widetilde\zeta].
 \hypertarget{tag-037P}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-additive-fibre-map}
\end{equation}
Its image lattice is exactly the one in the statement, with index
$\det S_N=N^2$.  In source coordinates the deck maps are
$\zeta\mapsto\zeta+(a,b)/N$, $(a,b)\in\mathbb Z^2/N\mathbb Z^2$;
they exponentiate to the phase action above.

For the clockwise cusp generator, the target clutch after base change
is $M_0^N$.  Write $M_0=I+R$, where
$R(a,b,c,d)=(0,0,b,-a)$ and $R^2=0$.  Then
\[
 M_0^N=I+NR,\qquad M_0^NS_N=S_NM_0.
\]
Both clutches fix the zero section, represented by $(1,1)$ after
exponentiation, and the map $\zeta\mapsto N\zeta$ preserves it.
Thus this identity also intertwines the affine clutches.  The induced
action on $\Lambda/S_N\Lambda$ is trivial, because every change under
$M_0^N$ is $N$ times a short period.  The deck group therefore acts on
the whole punctured relative family.

Finally, $P_N$ preserves every ray and sends $D_p$ to $D_p$.
On $D_0$ its induced cocharacter map on
$N'/\mathbb Z(0,0,1)$ is multiplication by $N$.  This is the map
$[N]\colon E_N\to E$ of degree $N^2$.  Its boundary charts have form
$(a,b)\mapsto(a^N,b^N)$, which gives ramification index $N$ along
each of the six boundary curves.  The normalization maps are the
inclusions of $D_0$ followed by the period quotient maps.
Equation \eqref{wb:cusp-cover-equivariance-computation} makes their
square commute.  In particular, each source conductor identification
by $\bar\lambda$ maps to the target identification by the same
$\bar\lambda$, including its holomorphic unit factors.  The two
translation orbits of maximal triangles are each preserved.  They
give the two triple-point classes.  Normalization is generically an
isomorphism, so the reduced central map has degree $N^2$.

At $N=1$, the two actions coincide, $P_1$ is the coordinate identity,
and $\kappa_1$ is its quotient.  The projection $N_0[1]\to N_0$ has
inverse $y\mapsto(y,f_0(y))$, which identifies $Q_1$ with the identity.
All ramification divisors and branch supports are empty, the local
fibre lengths equal their generic ranks, and $S_1=I$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[The cusp cover and the original base]
\hypertarget{tag-037Y}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-global-scope}
The maps of Theorem~\ref{wb:cusp-cover-extension-theorem} have targets
$N_0$ and $N_0[N]$, with total degrees $N^3$ and $N^2$, respectively.
They are related by
\[
 Q_N(x)=(\kappa_N(x),f_N(x)),\qquad
 f_0\kappa_N=\rho_Nf_N,\qquad \rho_N(v)=v^N.
\]
For $N>1$, the degree $N^2>1$ excludes a normalization morphism to
the normal target $N_0[N]$.  At $N=1$, the coordinate identity and
the isomorphism $y\mapsto(y,f_0(y))$ identify both factors with
identities.

For $N>1$, the connected regular-fibre cover with image
\[
 \Lambda_N=\mathbb Z\langle\widehat\gamma,\widehat u,
                       N\widehat w,N\widehat\delta\rangle
\]
does not extend as a fibrewise covering over the original regular
base $B^\circ$, and consequently does not extend over that same base
through both finite fillings.  Indeed, the monodromy matrix $A_1$
satisfies
\[
 A_1\widehat u=-\widehat w+\widehat\delta,\qquad
 S_N^{-1}A_1S_N\widehat u=(0,0,-1/N,1/N)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Thus $A_1\widehat u\notin\Lambda_N$.  A connected fibrewise torus
cover over $B^\circ$ induces an inclusion of integral $H_1$ local
systems; its image lattice must be invariant under every base loop.
This necessary condition fails for $\Lambda_N$.

On the changed local cusp base the intertwining is instead
$M_0^NS_N=S_NM_0$, as proved in the theorem.  The obstruction just
given concerns the original base and its prescribed fibre subgroup.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Comparison of the two source actions]
\hypertarget{tag-0382}{}\label{wb:cusp-cover-naive-action-failure}
On the compatible discs of Theorem~\ref{wb:cusp-cover-extension-theorem},
let $\Psi^{\mathrm{un}}_{\bar\lambda}$ be the source action obtained
from \eqref{wb:cusp-cover-target-action} by replacing $t$ with $v$.
Direct substitution gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_N\Psi^{\mathrm{un}}_{\bar\lambda}(\xi,v)
   &=\bigl(c_{\bar\lambda}(v)^N
               v^{NB_0\bar\lambda}\xi^N,v^N\bigr),\\
 \Psi_{\bar\lambda}P_N(\xi,v)
   &=\bigl(c_{\bar\lambda}(v^N)
               v^{NB_0\bar\lambda}\xi^N,v^N\bigr).
 \end{aligned}
\]
More precisely, the first map is the second followed by multiplication
in the two fibre coordinates by
\[
 d_{\bar\lambda}(v)
   =\exp\!\bigl(2\pi i\{NC(v)-C(v^N)\}\bar\lambda\bigr).
\]
Consequently the unmodified action is equivariant exactly when
$c_{\bar\lambda}(v)^N=c_{\bar\lambda}(v^N)$ for every
$\bar\lambda\in\bar\Lambda$.  Equality on the dense torus extends
through all toric charts.

The source factor \eqref{wb:cusp-cover-source-factor} satisfies
\[
 (c^{(N)}_{\bar\lambda}(v))^N=c_{\bar\lambda}(v^N),\qquad
 c^{(N)}_{\bar\lambda+\bar\mu}
   =c^{(N)}_{\bar\lambda}c^{(N)}_{\bar\mu}.
\]
Both identities follow from its holomorphic logarithm
$2\pi iC(v^N)\bar\lambda/N$.  At $N=1$ the two actions coincide
for every holomorphic $C$.

For $N>1$, the equality criterion can also be written
\[
 C(v)=C_0\text{ is constant},\qquad
 (N-1)C_0\in\operatorname{Mat}_2(\mathbb Z).
\]
To prove this, equality for the two basis vectors of $\bar\Lambda$
makes every entry of $NC(v)-C(v^N)$ integer-valued.  It is a
holomorphic matrix on a connected disc, so it is constant, with value
$(N-1)C(0)$.  Write $C(v)=\sum_{k\geq0}C_kv^k$.
The positive coefficients satisfy $NC_k=0$ when $N\nmid k$ and
$NC_k=C_{k/N}$ when $N\mid k$.  Writing $k=N^a k_0$ with
$N\nmid k_0$ proves $C_k=0$ for every $k>0$.  Conversely, a constant
$C_0$ with the displayed integrality has $d_{\bar\lambda}=1$.
In this equality case, putting $L=(N-1)C_0$ gives the exact relation
between the two source actions:
\[
 \Psi^{\mathrm{un}}_{\bar\lambda}
   =m_{\exp(2\pi iL\bar\lambda/N)}
       \circ\Psi^{(N)}_{\bar\lambda}.
\]
Here $m_\eta(\xi,v)=(\eta\xi,v)$, and the multiplier lies in the
deck group $\mu_N^2$ of the relative toric power map.
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[Higher smash powers]
\hypertarget{tag-038T}{}\label{wb:cusp-s12-all-higher-smashes-null}
For every continuous based map $g:S^6\to S^3$ and every integer
$r\geq2$, the ordered external smash
\[
 g^{\wedge r}:S^{6r}\longrightarrow S^{3r}
\]
is based null-homotopic.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Use the cube models $C_d=[0,1]^d/\partial[0,1]^d$ and the ordered
concatenation homeomorphisms of
\cref{wb:cusp-cone-angle-forgotten-sphere-carriers}.
Write $\mu_{d_1,\ldots,d_k}$ for concatenation of these blocks;
its inverse splits the nonboundary coordinates into the same blocks
and sends the quotient basepoint to the smash basepoint.
By \cref{wb:cusp-s12-full-carrier-null}, there is a based homotopy
$H_2:C_{12}\times I\to C_6$ with initial map
$\mu_{3,3}(g\wedge g)\mu_{6,6}^{-1}$ and constant terminal map.
This proves the case $r=2$.

For $r>2$, split the source by
$a_r=\mu_{12,6,\ldots,6}^{-1}$ and put
$b_r=\mu_{6,3,\ldots,3}$, with $r-2$ remaining blocks in each.
Define
\[
 H_r\bigl(a_r^{-1}[w,u_3,\ldots,u_r],s\bigr)
 =b_r[H_2(w,s),g(u_3),\ldots,g(u_r)].
\]
The fat wedge maps to the target basepoint at every time, so the
formula descends continuously to $C_{6r}\times I$.
Indeed, the product-to-smash quotient is a closed surjection between
compact Hausdorff spaces, and its product with $I$ is also a quotient.
Concatenating the first two blocks and then the remaining blocks is
the same map as concatenating all blocks at once. Thus
$H_r(-,0)=\mu_{3,\ldots,3}g^{\wedge r}\mu_{6,\ldots,6}^{-1}$.
At time one the first smash factor is the basepoint, so $H_r(-,1)=*$;
the source basepoint remains fixed for every time.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{The postcomposition and its scope.}
\hypertarget{tag-038W}{}\label{wb:cusp-s12-nullity-scope}
Write $K=S^1\times\overline T^2$ and
\[
 \mathcal A=([0,\epsilon]\times K)/
 (\{0\}\times K=v_0,\ \{\epsilon\}\times K=v_1),
 \qquad B=\Sigma_{\mathrm{red},\epsilon}Z_2.
\]
The two poles in $\mathcal A$ are distinct, and its basepoint is $v_0$.
For the coordinate-skeleton collapse $c:\overline T^2\to Z_2$, the
continuous based map
\[
 p=\widehat p_2:\mathcal A\longrightarrow B,
 \qquad [r,z,a]\longmapsto[r,c(a)]
\]
sends both poles to the reduced-suspension basepoint and satisfies
$\widehat q_3=pq_2$.  Let $d:C_6\to X$ be the fixed based source
identification, let $\phi:B\to C_3$ be the target homeomorphism of
\cref{wb:cusp-cone-angle-forgotten-sphere-carriers}, and let $\mu$
denote the ordered cube concatenations used there.  Put
\[
 Q=(q_2\wedge q_2)(d\wedge d)\mu_{6,6}^{-1},\qquad
 P=\mu_{3,3}(\phi\wedge\phi)(p\wedge p).
\]
Thus $Q:C_{12}\to\mathcal A\wedge\mathcal A$ and
$P:\mathcal A\wedge\mathcal A\to C_6$, with literal equality
$PQ=\widehat q_3^{\wedge2}$ under these identifications: both send
$[x_1,x_2]$ to $[pq_2(x_1),pq_2(x_2)]$ and send the fat wedge to the
basepoint.  Postcomposition therefore gives the homomorphism
\[
 P_*:\pi_{12}(\mathcal A\wedge\mathcal A,*)\longrightarrow
       \pi_{12}(C_6,*),\qquad [f]\longmapsto[Pf],
 \qquad P_*[Q]=0
\]
by \cref{wb:cusp-s12-full-carrier-null}.  The basepoint in the source
group is the image of
$(\{v_0\}\times\mathcal A)\cup(\mathcal A\times\{v_0\})$.
Postcomposition respects addition because it commutes with the
source-sphere pinch.

This homomorphism has a nonzero kernel in the indicated dimension.
Here are the maps that exhibit it.  Choose the coordinate basepoint
$a_*\in K^{(1)}\subset\overline T^2$.  On the unreduced suspension
$S(S^1)\cong C_2$, based at its zero pole, define
\[
 j_2[r,z]=[r,z,a_*],\qquad r_2[r,z,a]=[r,z].
\]
These formulas respect both pole quotients, and
$r_2j_2=\mathrm{id}_{C_2}$ and $pj_2=*$ exactly.  The sphere
homeomorphism, after $s=r/\epsilon$, is
$[s,e^{i\theta}]\mapsto
(\sin(\pi s)\cos\theta,\sin(\pi s)\sin\theta,\cos(\pi s))$;
off the poles its inverse reads $s=\pi^{-1}\arccos x_3$ and the
phase of $x_1+ix_2$.

For completeness, an explicit map supplies the required
four-sphere homotopy retract.  Give $K=(S^1)^3$ its product cell
structure and, for each nonempty $I\subset\{0,1,2\}$, let
$k_I:K\to\bigwedge_{i\in I}S^1=C_{|I|}$ be the ordered coordinate
projection followed by the product-to-smash quotient.  Order these
subsets as
\[
 \{0\},\{1\},\{2\},\{0,1\},\{0,2\},\{1,2\},\{0,1,2\}
\]
and put $V=\bigvee_{I\ne\varnothing}\Sigma_{\mathrm{red}}C_{|I|}$.
On the $j$th closed radial subinterval define
\[
 F:\mathcal A\longrightarrow V,\qquad
 F[r,k]=\iota_{I_j}[7r/\epsilon-(j-1),k_{I_j}(k)],
 \quad (j-1)\epsilon/7\leq r\leq j\epsilon/7.
\]
At every adjoining endpoint both expressions are the wedge
basepoint, so finite pasting and quotient descent make $F$ a
continuous based map.  The product cells $e_I$ of $K$ have zero
cellular boundary.  Suspending them gives
$H_2(\mathcal A)=\mathbb Z^3$, $H_3(\mathcal A)=\mathbb Z^3$ and
$H_4(\mathcal A)=\mathbb Z$; the edge joining the two poles has
boundary $v_1-v_0$, so $H_1(\mathcal A)=0$ and $H_0(\mathcal A)=\mathbb Z$.
All other homology groups vanish.  For $|I|=|J|$, the map $k_I$ on
$e_J$ has degree $1$ for $I=J$ and $0$ otherwise, since in the latter
case a projected coordinate is the basepoint.  Each increasing
radial reparametrization has degree $1$.  Hence $F_*$ is the identity
matrix in these bases and the corresponding sphere bases of $V$.
The two overlapping cones on the connected space $K$ show that
$\mathcal A$ is simply connected; $V$ is a wedge of spheres of
dimensions at least two.  Thus $F$ is a homotopy equivalence by
\cite[Corollary~4.33, pp.~367--368]{Hatcher2002}.

Choose a based homotopy inverse $G:V\to\mathcal A$.  An initially
unbased inverse can be moved at the basepoint along a path by the
CW homotopy extension property.  The basepoint tracks of its two
inverse homotopies are loops in simply connected spaces, so filling
those loops and applying the same relative extension property makes
both homotopies based.  Their inverse relations determine the based
class of $G$, since $G\simeq G(FG')\simeq G'$ for any other such
inverse.  For the inclusion $i_4:C_4\to V$ of its last summand and
its wedge projection $p_4$, set $j_4=Gi_4$ and $r_4=p_4F$.  Then
$r_4j_4\simeq\mathrm{id}_{C_4}$ through based maps.  Consequently
\[
 J=(j_4\wedge j_2)\mu_{4,2}^{-1}:C_6\longrightarrow
        \mathcal A\wedge\mathcal A,
 \qquad R=\mu_{4,2}(r_4\wedge r_2)
\]
satisfy $RJ\simeq\mathrm{id}_{C_6}$ through based maps and $PJ=*$
exactly.  Take $h:C_{12}\to C_6$ representing the nonzero element
of $\pi_{12}(S^6)=\mathbb Z/2$
\cite[p.~339]{Hatcher2002}.  Then
\[
 \beta=[Jh]\ne0,\qquad R_*\beta=[h],\qquad P_*\beta=0.
\]
This proves noninjectivity of this exact $P_*$.  The native class
$[Q]$ belongs to its kernel; the construction assigns no further
value to $[Q]$ and makes no identification of $\beta$ with $[Q]$.

The same initial maps retain the point-set and metric properties
proved in \cref{wb:cusp-cone-angle-forgotten-sphere-carriers}.
In particular, $PQ$ is the continuous surjective quotient in that
theorem.  At height $r_T$ its restriction factors through
$Q_T^2\to S_T^2\wedge S_T^2$ and the two height sections
$j_{r_T}:Z_2\to B$, $z\mapsto[r_T,z]$, followed by the same $\phi$
and $\mu_{3,3}$.  The inverse of each section on its image reads the
$z$ coordinate.  For $T-C>4R$, the intrinsic entire-ball isometry is
$u\mapsto[\widetilde b_T+u]$, first in $Q_T^2$ and then in its
collapsed-fat-wedge quotient; its inverse is the unique period lift
of norm at most $R$ relative to $\widetilde b_T$.  These are the
moving embedded four-spheres and pointed $\mathbb R^4$ limits of the
same initial map of the based null-homotopy.

For the four-circle carrier, the corresponding restriction is
$F_T^4\to C_T^4\to C_T^{\wedge4}$, followed in each factor by
$[u]\mapsto[u/\ell_T]$, its height section and the ordered
$\mu_{2,2,2,2}$.  The inverse circle coordinate multiplies by
$\ell_T$.  For $\ell_T>4R$, the same formula
$u\mapsto[\widetilde b_T+u]$ and its unique period-lift inverse give
the second entire-ball isometry.  Smashing the based homotopy in
\cref{mapsIII:angle-forgotten-one-copy-null} four times gives
$[x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4],s\mapsto
[H_\gamma(x_1,s),H_\gamma(x_2,s),H_\gamma(x_3,s),H_\gamma(x_4,s)]$.
It descends through the fat wedge at every time, starts at this same
four-circle carrier and ends at the constant map.  Thus both moving
four-sphere families and their intrinsic limits occur at the
specified initial quotient maps of based null-homotopies.

\paragraph{The one-copy invariant and its computed value}
\hypertarget{tag-038X}{}\label{wb:cusp-s12-one-copy-invariant}
\StatementRecord{wb:cusp-s12-one-copy-invariant}{proved}{038X}{\SeriesRef{wb:cusp-null:thm}; \cite[Theorem~5.41(b), p.~573, and pp.~577--578]{HatcherSpectralSequences}}

The proof does not need to determine the one-copy class
\([g]\in\pi_6(S^3)\cong\mathbb Z/12\).  Toda's suspension calculation
identifies \(\pi_6(S^3)\) with the even subgroup of the stable three-stem;
Hatcher gives an integral Serre-spectral-sequence derivation of the same
injectivity and identifies twice the stable Hopf--\(\nu\) generator with a
generator of the suspended \(\mathbb Z/12\)-summand
\cite[Theorem~5.41(b), p.~573, and pp.~577--578]{HatcherSpectralSequences}.
Thus, after choosing a stable generator \(\nu_9\), there is a unique
\(a\in\mathbb Z/12\) such that
\begin{equation}
 [E^6g]=2a\nu_9\in\pi_{12}(S^9)\cong\mathbb Z/24.
 \hypertarget{tag-038Z}{}\label{wb:cusp-s12-sixfold-suspension-class}
\end{equation}
Because \(a\mapsto2a\) embeds \(\mathbb Z/12\) as the even subgroup of
\(\mathbb Z/24\), \(E^6g\) is null-homotopic if and only if \(g\) is
null-homotopic.  Thus the one-copy class and its sixfold suspension are the
same integer modulo \(12\). It is now zero by Theorem~\ref{wb:cusp-null:thm}.

The exact geometric invariant which computes \(a\) is also identifiable.
Choose \(0<r_0<\epsilon\) and
\(u_0\in\overline T^2\setminus K^{(1)}\), and let
\(y_0=[r_0,c(u_0)]\) lie in the open three-cell of
\(\Sigma_rS^2\).  From the literal formula for \(q_2\),
\begin{equation}
 g^{-1}(y_0)
 =\{x\in f^{-1}(|t|=r_0):\overline\pi_f(x)=u_0\}.
 \hypertarget{tag-038Y}{}\label{wb:cusp-s12-regular-inverse-image}
\end{equation}
The fibre of \(\overline\pi\) is the two-torus defined by
\(K_\Lambda=\mathbb Z\langle\widehat w,\widehat\delta\rangle\), and the
cusp monodromy fixes both \(\widehat w\) and \(\widehat\delta\).  Therefore
\eqref{wb:cusp-s12-regular-inverse-image} is the mapping torus of an affine translation of the kernel torus,
which is diffeomorphic to \(S^1\times T^2\cong T^3\): if the translation is
\(k\mapsto k+v\), choose a real lift \(\widetilde v\); the map
\([\theta,k]\mapsto(e^{2\pi i\theta},k+\theta\widetilde v)\) respects
\((1,k)\sim(0,k+v)\) and has the inverse obtained by subtracting
\(\theta\widetilde v\). After choosing a smooth chart in the open
target cell, the differential of \(g\) supplies its normal three-framing.
Pontryagin--Thom identifies the stabilized class of \(g\) with the framed
bordism class of this specifically framed \(T^3\).  Since stabilization on
\(\pi_6(S^3)\) is injective, computing that framing class computes \(a\)
exactly.  The unframed diffeomorphism type \(T^3\), point-set surjectivity,
and the zero ordinary homology map do not compute \(a\).

\paragraph{The one-copy coefficient and the framed fibre.}
\hypertarget{tag-038X}{}\label{wb:cusp-s12-one-copy-invariant}
The pairing theorem \cref{wb:cusp-s12-full-carrier-null} applies to
every class in $\pi_6(S^3)$, so its application to the native map
requires no prior value of that class.  We now describe and compute
the one-copy coefficient.  In homotopy groups, $g$ denotes the exact
composite
\[
 C_6\xrightarrow{d}X\xrightarrow{g}
 \Sigma_{\mathrm{red},\epsilon}Z_2\xrightarrow{\phi}C_3,
 \qquad \phi[r,c(u_1,u_2)]=[r/\epsilon,u_1,u_2],
\]
with the fixed based identifications of
\cref{wb:cusp-cone-angle-forgotten-sphere-carriers}.

The suspension calculation in
\cite[Theorem~5.41(b), p.~573, and pp.~577--578]{HatcherSpectralSequences}
gives an injection
$\pi_6(S^3)=\mathbb Z/12\to\pi_7(S^4)=\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z/12$
onto the torsion summand.  The next suspension is the quotient by
the relation $2e=t$, where $e$ and $t$ generate the two summands.
Its explicit coordinate map is
\[
 L:\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z/12\longrightarrow\mathbb Z/24,
 \qquad(n,[m]_{12})\longmapsto[n+2m]_{24}.
\]
Its kernel is $\langle(2,[-1]_{12})\rangle$: the congruence
$n+2m\equiv0\pmod{24}$ gives $n=2k$ and $[m]_{12}=[-k]_{12}$.
The inverse on this quotient sends $[j]_{24}$ to the class of
$(j,0)$; changing $j$ by $24$ adds $12(2,-1)$, and
$(n,m)-(n+2m,0)=m(-2,1)$ proves both inverse identities.
The restriction to the torsion summand is therefore
$[m]_{12}\mapsto[2m]_{24}$, with inverse
$[2m]_{24}\mapsto[m]_{12}$ on its even image.
The next four suspensions are isomorphisms by
\cite[Corollary~4.24]{Hatcher2002}, in the strict ranges
$8<9$, $9<11$, $10<13$ and $11<15$.  Thus $E^6$ is injective
and its image is exactly the even subgroup of $\pi_{12}(S^9)$.

For the chosen generator $\nu_9$, let $\gamma$ be the unique class
with $E^6\gamma=2\nu_9$.  It has order $12$.  There is a unique
$a\in\mathbb Z/12$ such that
\begin{equation}
 [E^6g]=2a\nu_9\in\pi_{12}(S^9)\cong\mathbb Z/24.
 \hypertarget{tag-038Z}{}\label{wb:cusp-s12-sixfold-suspension-class}
\end{equation}
More precisely, the coefficient homomorphism
\[
 \operatorname{coef}_{\nu_9}:\pi_6(S^3)\longrightarrow\mathbb Z/12,
 \qquad x\longmapsto a\quad\text{where }E^6x=2a\nu_9,
\]
has inverse $[a]_{12}\mapsto a\gamma$.  The two inverse identities
follow by applying the injective $E^6$ and the inverse on its even
image.  Consequently $[g]=0$ precisely when $[E^6g]=0$ and precisely
when $a=0$.  For the native map these values are zero by
\cref{wb:cusp-null:thm}.

These suspensions use the ordered cube homeomorphisms $\mu_{p,q}$,
whose inverse splits the coordinates into blocks of lengths $p,q$.
The left and right representatives are
\[
 E_L=\mu_{6,3}(\mathrm{id}_{C_6}\wedge g)\mu_{6,6}^{-1},
 \qquad
 E_R=\mu_{3,6}(g\wedge\mathrm{id}_{C_6})\mu_{6,6}^{-1}.
\]
For the block interchanges, evaluation on representatives gives
$E_L=\tau_{3,6}E_R\tau_{6,6}$.  The degrees of the two interchanges
are $(-1)^{18}=1$ and $(-1)^{36}=1$, respectively.  The degree
classification \cite[Corollary~4.25]{Hatcher2002} makes both based
homotopic to the identity.  Thus these two actual models give the
same coefficient convention.

For $0<r_0<\epsilon$ and
$u_0\in\overline T^2\setminus K^{(1)}$, put $y_0=[r_0,c(u_0)]$.
The literal map on the open cell gives the entire inverse image
\begin{equation}
 g^{-1}(y_0)
 =\{x\in f^{-1}(|t|=r_0):\overline\pi_f(x)=u_0\}.
 \hypertarget{tag-038Y}{}\label{wb:cusp-s12-regular-inverse-image}
\end{equation}
The real marking has local coordinates $(r,\theta,v_1,v_2,u_1,u_2)$,
and there $g=(r,u_1,u_2)$ in the target open-cell coordinates.
Hence $y_0$ is a regular value.  To identify its full fibre, choose
a real lift $\widetilde u^0$ of $u_0$, set
$p^0=B_0\widetilde u^0$ and $T_0=-\log r_0/(2\pi)$, and use
$s=\theta+iT_0$.  In $\zeta=v+Z(s)\widetilde u^0$ the monodromy
$Z(s+1)=Z(s)+B_0$ gives exactly
$(1,v)\sim(0,v+p^0)$.  This is the affine translation of the kernel
torus with lattice
$K_\Lambda=\mathbb Z\langle\widehat w,\widehat\delta\rangle$;
the monodromy fixes its two lattice generators.  The coordinates
$\alpha=v+\theta p^0\pmod{\mathbb Z^2}$ agree at the gluing and give
the product parametrization
\[
 t=r_0e^{2\pi i\theta},\qquad
 x_j=e^{2\pi i\alpha_j}r_0^{p^0_j}
       e^{2\pi i(C(t)\widetilde u^0)_j},\quad j=1,2,
\]
followed by the original period quotient.  Its inverse reads
$t/r_0$ and $\alpha=v+\theta p^0$.  Replacing $\theta$ by
$\theta+n$ replaces $v$ by $v-np^0$, and integer logarithmic
changes alter $\alpha$ only by $\mathbb Z^2$.  The long-period
translation selects the lift $u=\widetilde u^0$ uniquely modulo the
kernel lattice.  These formulas are smooth inverse maps, proving
that the whole fibre is the embedded $S^1\times T^2\cong T^3$.

The inverse differential of the ordered coordinates $(r,c_1,c_2)$
gives its normal three-framing.  A complement to the tangent bundle
makes this inverse literal; changing the complement changes its
lifts by tangential vectors and gives a homotopy of framed normal
bundles.  A smaller closed tubular neighbourhood has compact
complement whose image misses $y_0$.  Relative smooth approximation
within half this positive image distance, fixed near the fibre and
the basepoint, therefore preserves the entire regular fibre and its
frame.  The based Pontryagin--Thom construction identifies this
framed fibre with $[g]$
\cite[\S7, Theorem~B and Lemma~4, pp.~43, 48--50]{CuspNullMilnor1965}.
In the right suspension model, an interior value $(y_0,z_0)$ has
fibre $g^{-1}(y_0)\times\{z_0\}$ and frame consisting of the original
triple followed by six coordinate normals.  In the left model the
order is six normals followed by that triple.  The displayed block
maps relate these framed products.  Their class is $E^6g$, and
$\operatorname{coef}_{\nu_9}$ recovers $a$ exactly.
The product framing calculation takes place on $X$ times the open
six-cell; precomposition by $d\wedge\mathrm{id}_{C_6}$ is the
displayed source map defining its sphere cohomotopy class.

Here is a framing comparison that proves what the unframed data
determine.  Take the particular embedded torus $N$ and bounding
derivative framing $\tau_0$ of \cref{wb:cusp-null:thm}.  We construct
two maps with this same embedded regular fibre and coefficients
$0$ and $1$, retaining the fixed $\nu_9$.  For this comparison,
$y_0$ denotes the particular regular value used in that theorem.

We specify the target coordinate change used in the construction.
Let $S^3_{\mathbb H}$ be the unit quaternions, based at $1$, and
write imaginary quaternions as vectors in $\mathbb R^3$.  Define
\[
 \mathcal Q(w)=\frac{|w|^2-1+2w}{1+|w|^2},\qquad
 h_i(t)=\lambda_i\frac{t-y_i}{t(1-t)},
\]
where $(y_1,y_2,y_3)$ are the cube coordinates of $\phi(y_0)$,
$\lambda_1=\epsilon y_1(1-y_1)/2$, and
$\lambda_i=y_i(1-y_i)/2$ for $i=2,3$.
The map $b:C_3\to S^3_{\mathbb H}$ sends an open-cube point
$(t_1,t_2,t_3)$ to $\mathcal Q(h_1(t_1),h_2(t_2),h_3(t_3))$ and
the basepoint to $1$.  Each $h_i$ is an increasing diffeomorphism
onto $\mathbb R$, since
\[
 h_i'(t)=\lambda_i
 \frac{(t-y_i)^2+y_i(1-y_i)}{t^2(1-t)^2}>0.
\]
The inverse of $b$ away from $1$ first takes
$w=\mathcal Q^{-1}(q)=\operatorname{Im}(q)/(1-\operatorname{Re}(q))$,
then in each coordinate takes the unique root of $h_i(t)=w_i$ in $(0,1)$.
At the cube boundary at least one $|h_i|$ tends to infinity, so
the map tends to $1$.  This proves the continuous quotient descent
and both inverse identities.  Moreover $b(\phi(y_0))=-1$ and the
derivative of $b\phi$ sends $(\partial_r,\partial_{c_1},\partial_{c_2})$
exactly to $(i,j,k)$ at $-1$.

Choose a framed tubular embedding
$\Phi:N\times D^3_\rho\to X$ with
$d_v\Phi(x,0)=\tau_0(x)$ and image disjoint from $x_0$.
For $r=|v|<\rho$, put
\[
 \sigma(r)=\exp\!\left(-\frac{r^2}{\rho^2-r^2}\right),\qquad
 q(v)=\frac{r^2-4\sigma(r)^2+4\sigma(r)v}{r^2+4\sigma(r)^2},
 \qquad q|_{\partial D^3_\rho}=1.
\]
This is $\mathcal Q(v/(2\sigma(r)))$.  The radial function
$r/(2\sigma(r))$ increases from $0$ to infinity, so $q$ induces a
homeomorphism $D^3_\rho/\partial D^3_\rho\to S^3_{\mathbb H}$.
Its inverse first applies $\mathcal Q^{-1}$ and then the inverse
radial function.  The formula is smooth and flat at the boundary,
has derivative $I$ at $0$, and takes only $0$ to $-1$.
It commutes with rotations of the imaginary coordinates.  Orient
$S^3_{\mathbb H}$ by $q$, so $(i,j,k)$ at $-1$ is positive; orient
$D^4$ to induce this boundary orientation.

Define $F_0(\Phi(x,v))=q(v)$ and $F_0=1$ outside the tube.  Its
full fibre at $-1$ is $N$ with frame $\tau_0$, so
$[F_0d]=b_*[g]=0$.  The conjugation map
$\operatorname{Ad}:S^3_{\mathbb H}\to\mathrm{SO}(3)$ is the double
cover with kernel $\{1,-1\}$: the rotation of angle $\vartheta$
about a unit imaginary axis $u$ is represented by
$\cos(\vartheta/2)+u\sin(\vartheta/2)$.
Based maps from $S^3$ and their based homotopies lift uniquely after
choosing the lift $1$, so this cover induces an isomorphism on
$\pi_3$.  Thus $\xi=[\operatorname{Ad}]$ is a generator.

In the boundary definition of $J$
\cite[\S4.1, p.~108]{CuspInvariantHatcherVB}, for a based map
$f:S^3\to\mathrm{SO}(3)$ the map
$Jf:\partial(D^4\times D^3_\rho)\to S^3_{\mathbb H}$ is
$q(f(x)v)$ on $S^3\times D^3_\rho$ and $1$ on
$D^4\times\partial D^3_\rho$.  The identity-family map $J1$
extends over the product by $q(v)$.  Pointwise multiplication and
source-pinch addition agree in $\pi_6(S^3_{\mathbb H})$: they have
the same unit and satisfy the interchange rule on cube loops.
Hence $[J\operatorname{Ad}]-[J1]$ is represented on the side by
\[
 xq(v)x^{-1}q(v)^{-1}.
\]
It equals $1$ on the cap and on $\{1\}\times D^3_\rho$, so it
descends to $S^3\wedge(D^3_\rho/\partial D^3_\rho)$.
The collapse from the boundary sphere has degree $+1$: its open
top cell has the same ordered tangent-then-normal coordinates.
The degree classification therefore identifies this commutator
with exactly $J\xi$ in these sphere conventions.  The classical
calculation states that $J\xi$ generates $\pi_6(S^3)=\mathbb Z/12$

\begin{theorem}[invariant-Chern original additive caps and their integral extension]\hypertarget{tag-02LT}{}\label{maps:src:D.2.51}
\StatementRecord{maps:src:D.2.51}{proved}{02LT}{\SeriesRef{maps:src:D.2.50}, \SeriesRef{maps:src:D.2.31}, \SeriesRef{maps:src:D.2.16}}


Let $K$ be the reduced central fibre of an original additive
Kodaira neighbourhood, of type
$II,III,IV,IV^*,III^*,I_1^*$ or $I_3^*$.
Write its rational components as $C_i$, its primitive
multiplicity vector as $\mu=(\mu_i)$, and let $\sigma$
be the actual component permutation induced by the section $Q$.
Let the original line bundle have invariant component degrees
$c_i$, so that
\[
                  \sigma c=c,\qquad \sum_i\mu_i c_i=0.
                                                        \tag{D.IC1}\hypertarget{tag-01ZY}{}\label{maps:eq:D.IC1}
\]
These include every corrected line bundle in \ref{maps:src:D.2.50}.
Let the component orbits be $O_1,\ldots,O_\rho$, with
lengths $l_j$ and common degrees $c_j$ on $O_j$.
For $c\ne0$ put
\[
                  g=\gcd_j(c_j),\qquad
                  h=\gcd_j(l_jc_j),
                                                        \tag{D.IC2}\hypertarget{tag-01ZZ}{}\label{maps:eq:D.IC2}
\]
where both gcds are positive. For the resulting original
six-dimensional cap $U$, there is an exact integral cellular
cone, with its actual circle-fibre and regular-area classes,
\[
\begin{gathered}
 C_0=\mathbb Z,\quad C_1=\mathbb Z^2,\quad
 C_2=\mathbb Z^v\oplus\mathbb Zt,\quad
 C_3=\mathbb Z^v\oplus\mathbb Z^v,\quad C_4=\mathbb Z^v,\\
 d_2=\begin{pmatrix}c^t&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 d_3=\begin{pmatrix}0&\sigma-I\\0&c^t\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 d_4=\begin{pmatrix}I-\sigma\\0\end{pmatrix}.
\end{gathered}                                             \tag{D.IC3}\hypertarget{tag-0200}{}\label{maps:eq:D.IC3}
\]
The degree-one generators are the scalar circle $\delta$
and a positive long circle $\gamma$. In particular
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccc}
i&0&1&2&3&4\\\hline
H_i(U;\mathbb Z)&\mathbb Z&
\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z/g&
\mathbb Z^{\rho-1}\oplus\mathbb Z/h&
\mathbb Z^{2\rho-1}&\mathbb Z^\rho .
\end{array}                                               \tag{D.IC4}\hypertarget{tag-0201}{}\label{maps:eq:D.IC4}
\]
Moreover $\pi_1(U)=\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z/g$.
When $c=0$, these groups are instead
\[
 (H_0,H_1,H_2,H_3,H_4)=
 (\mathbb Z,\mathbb Z^2,\mathbb Z^{\rho+1},
                         \mathbb Z^{2\rho},\mathbb Z^\rho).
                                                        \tag{D.IC5}\hypertarget{tag-0202}{}\label{maps:eq:D.IC5}
\]
The actual regular-fibre torus $\delta\wedge\gamma$
maps to the class of $t$ in \eqref{maps:eq:D.IC3}, which generates
\emph{all} of the cyclic torsion $\mathbb Z/h$ when
$c\ne0$. The elliptic tori crossed with $\delta$ map
to zero. The complex elliptic area maps to the literal
cycle $(\mu,0)$ in \eqref{maps:eq:D.IC3}.

Let $B$ be the elliptic monodromy, $q$ its marked
$Q$-cocycle, and $z=(B-I)^{-1}q$. Put
\[
        q_Q=\gcd_j(l_j\mu_j)
             =\operatorname{ord}(\overline Q).
                                                        \tag{D.IC6}\hypertarget{tag-0203}{}\label{maps:eq:D.IC6}
\]
The actual logarithm $z$ has exact denominator $q_Q$.
For $c\ne0$, the full regular-fibre image in $H_2(U)$
is $\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z/h$ with free cokernel
of rank $\rho-2$. For $c=0$ it is a primitive
$\mathbb Z^2$ with free cokernel of rank $\rho-1$.
In both cases this is already the full boundary image.
Consequently the full boundary kernel projects onto
all of $\operatorname{Fix}(A)$ in the Wang sequence;
there is no omitted finite normal index.

If $h=1$, these facts determine the complete marked
local kernels. In the regular basis
$(e_1,e_2,\delta,\gamma)$ the actual fibre kernel is
\[
 \ker\bigl(q_Q(1,0,z_2,0,-z_1,0):\mathbb Z^6\to\mathbb Z\bigr),
                                                        \tag{D.IC7}\hypertarget{tag-0204}{}\label{maps:eq:D.IC7}
\]
where the six coordinates have their usual increasing
exterior order. Both literal fixed-normal tori bound.
The cap kills every vertical fundamental-group
coordinate and retains the primitive $\gamma$.
This includes the canonical new corrected star degrees
\[
 \begin{array}{c|c}
 I_1^*&(1,1,0,0,-1,0)\\
 I_3^*&(1,1,0,0,-1,0,0,0)
 \end{array}
                                                        \tag{D.IC8}\hypertarget{tag-0205}{}\label{maps:eq:D.IC8}
\]
for component classes $P=Q=2$ in $\mathbb Z/4$.
Their actual permutation has two paired outer orbits
and fixed inner components, and $g=h=1$.

For $h>1$, \eqref{maps:eq:D.IC3}--\eqref{maps:eq:D.IC6} do not by themselves specify
the torsion corrections of the two mixed
elliptic--gamma tori and the second fixed-normal torus.
The theorem does not replace those marked columns by
their saturation. In particular it does not supply an
unrestricted global gluing algorithm for those caps.

\end{theorem}
